#770. Is Cristiano Ronaldo Retiring? What His Portugal Announcement Means

Cristiano Ronaldo confirmed he was retiring from international soccer after 23 years with Portugal's National Team: "Today, the time has come to pass it on to the future."

Cristiano Ronaldo is kicking off a new chapter in his life.

More than 20 years after the soccer player made his debut for Portugal's National Team, he announced his international retirement with an emotional reflection on his legendary career.

"To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team," Ronaldo began in his Nov. 5 Instagram video. "I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years, I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world."

"Today, the time has come to pass it on to the future," he continued. "It was not an easy decision because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart. A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end."

Although the team's all-time top scorer is blowing the whistle on his international career, he will continue playing at the club level with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.

As Ronaldo—who holds the men's all-time global scoring record with 146 goals over 234 matches—expressed gratitude for his legacy, he also reflected on the most important lessons he is taking with him off the field.

"I learned a few very simple things," he explained in the video, "goals fade. Trophies end up in museums. Records are eventually broken. But there is something that time can never erase: the place we hold in people's hearts."

"When I look back at everything with the national team, I don't just see the matches, goals, records or trophies," he said. "I see millions of Portuguese people I have never met, but who became part of my life. Because, at the end of the day, football is so much bigger than a game. Football is about people."

The athlete shared a special message for his Portugal teammates, including Real Madrid's Bernardo Silva, as well as his former Manchester United teammates Bruno Fernandes and Rúben Dias.

"Thank you for every run, for every embrace, for every argument, for every silence before stepping onto the pitch," Ronaldo said, "for every victory we celebrated together, and every defeat that made us stronger. I had the privilege of being your captain, but no captain walks alone. You will always be part of my story."

Though he and head coach Jorge Jesus had a falling out earlier this season—which led to Ronaldo being slapped with a 30-day suspension and a $285 fine for walking out of Portugal's training camp over a dispute about his playing time—the athlete thanked everyone behind the scenes. (Jesus addressed the spat in a statement, noting that he was going to "think about the Portuguese national team" and had "nothing more to say.”)

Ronaldo emphasized, "Many of you never appeared in the photographs, but without you, none of those photographs would be possible."

He also put a spotlight on his wife Georgina Rodríguez, their 9-year-old twins Eva and Mateo, and kids Alana, 8, and Bella, 4.

"To my family, thank you for sharing this dream with me," he said. "Thank you for understanding the absences, the sacrifices and the moments when the national team had to take up a space in my life that also belonged to you. If I came this far, it was because we always walked hand in hand."

Following the announcement, the team shared its own Nov. 5 statement, thanking Ronaldo for his "absolutely extraordinary career" and noting that there will be a "fitting tribute" for his departure.

"Every drop of sweat, every decisive goal, and every captain's armband worn with pride on the field reflected his unconditional love for our jersey," the message read. "His dedication and legacy transcend the four lines of the pitch."

"Cristiano Ronaldo has elevated Portugal's name and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps, being, for many of us, the best player of all time," it continued. “Thank you for everything, CAPTAIN! This will always be your home!"

As Ronaldo focuses on what's next, keep reading for a closer look at his game-winning family.

When Cristiano Ronaldo met Georgina Rodríguez in 2016 at a Gucci store in Madrid where she was working as a sales assistant, No. 7 didn't dare think he'd met the one.

He had previously acknowledged that, while there were plenty of women eager to date him, he was aware that many of them had ulterior motives.

"To speak serious, it is not easy," Ronaldo said on the U.K.'s Jonathan Ross Show in November 2015, months after he and Irina Shayk ended a five-year relationship. "I know 50 percent approach just for interest. It's normal, not just me, but all the people who are famous, they have these kinds of problems."

So when he started dating Georgina, "I didn't expect it, honestly," Ronaldo said in the Netflix series I Am Georgina. "But after a while I felt that she was the woman of my life."

He often picked her up after work and, as she recalled in the series, per the show's Spanish-to-English translation, "I remember once in a Bugatti. My coworkers went crazy. They get there on the bus, and I would leave in a Bugatti. I mean people couldn't believe it."

But instead of ferrying her to an equally attention-grabbing location, they'd usually just go home, Cristiano said, "into our own world."

Georgina described her partner as "great" and "a very normal guy," noting, "I dreamed of having a Prince Charming by my side and now I have him."

For years her official title (Mrs.? Princess?) was unclear, Ronaldo publicly referring to Georgina as his wife long before she said "I do" to a massive diamond engagement ring in August 2025.

Cristiano Ronaldo Jr. was born on June 17, 2010, while his dad was in South Africa playing in the World Cup. But the athlete flew immediately to see his firstborn child as soon as Portugal was knocked out of the tournament—and proceeded to raise him as a single dad.

"It is with great joy and emotion that I inform I have recently become father to a baby boy,” he shared in a statement on his social media accounts at the time. "As agreed with the baby’s mother, who prefers to have her identity kept confidential, my son will be under my exclusive guardianship."

Cristiano Jr. has been front and center in his father's life ever since, traveling all over the world with him and, naturally, picking up the beautiful game.

The teen trained at the youth clubs of whichever team Ronaldo was playing for, including Real Madrid and Juventus. And when the family moved to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in 2023 after the five-time Ballon d'Or winner signed a contract worth $200 million a year with Al Nassr FC, Cristiano Jr. subsequently started playing in the team's youth academy.

But though his eldest child has designs on playing professionally, which Ronaldo would admittedly love, he insists he's not pressuring Cristiano Jr. to make that dream a reality.

"This generation, it's difficult to tell them something and let them do it...They see me every day what I do, at home, or in training or in a game," the athlete said on the Rio Ferdinand Presents podcast in September 2024. "They say, 'My dad works a lot every time.' They see that."

As for his son, he continued, "He has pressure on him already being the son of Cristiano...Let him do his things. I hope so, in the future, he can be a professional player. If he's not a player, does another job, I always will support him. We can't make pressure on our sons because we are famous."

And yet it's looking good, with his son helping lead Portugal's under-16 squad to a win over England in the Federations Cup Tournament in November 2025.

"I love being a mom," Georgina captioned pics celebrating his victory. "I am very proud of my big boy."

While Georgina didn't come into Ronaldo's life until his son was 6, she considers Cristiano Jr. as much her son as she does the kids they later had together.

When the lad turned 14 in 2024, she posted to her Instagram, "Happy Birthday to my big boy...I love you to the moon and baaacccckkkk." (She also wasn't kidding about big: In the video she shared of him opening presents, the teen was taller than his mom. And the proud owner of a Louis Vuitton roller bag.)

Ronaldo was about seven months into his relationship with Georgina when he welcomed twins Mateo and Eva Maria Ronaldo via surrogate on June 8, 2017.

"So happy to be able to hold the two new loves of my life," he captioned the first photo he shared of his infant son and daughter a few weeks later.

And so Georgina became mom to Ronaldo's three eldest children, telling Vogue Mexico in 2024, "Being a mother is the best thing that's ever happened to me and my absolute priority. Every moment I spend with my family is when I'm happiest and most realized."

Georgina gave birth to daughter Alana Martina Ronaldo, her first child with Ronaldo, on Nov. 12, 2017. And she's already co-captain of the whole family team.

In Netflix's I Am Georgina, which premiered in 2022, Ronaldo asked Alana at the dinner table what she wanted to be when she grew up, and she hilariously pushed back.

"Nothing," she said in Spanish. "Nothing. I wanna stay at home and be at peace."

Her dad had a good laugh, then predicted that she would be an actress. When she instead mimed taking photos, he suggested "Netflix producer," and Alana heartily agreed, clapping her hands.

Cristiano and Georgina welcomed twins Bella Esmeralda Ronald and Ángel Ronaldo on April 18, 2022, but Ángel died at birth.

"This year I had the best and the worst moment of my life in an instant," Georgina reflected on a season two episode of her series that dropped in 2023.

"Life is hard," she continued. "Life goes on...I have reasons to move on and be strong. Cris really encouraged me to continue with my agenda. He said, 'Gio, get on with life. It'll do you good.'"

At the same time, Ronaldo has said that, after having to share with their other children the devastating news that Bella's twin wouldn't be coming home, they talk about Ángel every day.

"The kids understand, we had shouts around the table and they say, 'Daddy, I did this for Ángel,' and they point to the sky," Ronaldo shared in a November 2022 interview with Piers Morgan.  "Which I like the most because he's part of their lives. I am not gonna lie to my kids, I say the truth, which was a difficult process."

Bella is happily thriving, Georgina sharing video of her youngest on her lap while they watched one of her sibling’s school performances in December 2024.

“Seeing my kids grow up happy and sharing moments with my family is my best blessing. I couldn't be happier with the wonderful family we've made," Georgina said in the Netflix series. "My kids are wonderful. I know it's bad to say it but they're perfect kids, they're a dream."

#769. English female coach Kaminski reaping rewards in Norway

Laura Kaminski guided Crystal Palace to the WSL 2 title in 2024

When English manager Laura Kaminski was approached to become the head coach of Norwegian club SK Brann in January, she could not turn it down.

She jumped at the opportunity to move abroad and develop her coaching skills and is even competing for a place in the Europa Cup quarter-finals next Wednesday.

It was a decision that paid off as 10 months later, she is celebrating a Norwegian league and cup double after a dream debut season.

"My time in the city [of Bergen] has been brilliant," the 38-year-old told BBC Sport.

"I can't go to the supermarket at the minute because so many people are stopping me to wish me congratulations, which is so nice.

"I'm over the moon and it was nice to get the title done before the last game so we can relax. I thought it was going to go right to the wire.

"It's been a competitive year. I've enjoyed every minute. We had a great night with all our fans, who were waiting for us to return from Oslo."

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Kaminski on the challenges for English coaches in WSL

Kaminski described it as a "hectic" year as she moved from London to Norway and away from her family to take on the Brann job.

The Englishwoman had spent over a year at Crystal Palace, where she led them to promotion to the Women's Super League in 2024.

She was sacked in February 2025 after a tough WSL season as Palace struggled to compete with better financially-backed clubs.

However, she is regarded as one of the country's brightest female managers and has added to her CV with her experiences in Norway.

"I've learned a lot. It's been chaotic - I counted that I have taken 65 flights in 11 months - so it's been exhausting, but what an experience!" added Kaminski.

"To go all the way up to the Arctic Circle and play away [games] in freezing cold conditions with horizontal snow, to beautiful days in Bergen.

"Palace was totally different to Brann. I'm at a club that expects to win the Toppserien [the Norwegian top-flight] as they believe they have invested the most.

"That's been a real challenge. The WSL is dominated by the favourites in the pack so it wasn't always the expectation to get three points against big teams [at Palace]."

Kaminski admits being away from loved ones is "hard" and she has had to be prepared to "make sacrifices" but Brann's trophy success makes it worth it.

She has also picked up new ideas for her coaching philosophy having experienced the high-risk, attack-minded football in Norway.

"Norwegian teams are almost guaranteed to concede every game because they play such attacking football with no fear, and a relentlessness to press," she added.

"That is a bit different to what I was used to. When I watched the tactical displays when I first came in, I was a little bit alarmed at what people were doing.

"But when you play against their sides, and against that [pressing], it is really difficult. It's given me a lot of fuel for the future.

"There are some really fit, fast and athletic players here. It's not a surprise that big, big clubs are coming in for them."

Laura Kaminski spent a year and a half at Crystal Palace

After a season in Norway, Kaminski believes she is a better coach.

She had spent over 15 years as an assistant manager at various clubs in the WSL 2 and WSL and a coaching role with England's under-19s before joining Palace.

But having added European experience to her CV, Kaminski hopes it will open the door to more opportunities in the future.

"I'd like to think I've got a well-rounded skillset to be able to manage at the top level. Right now, my focus is on Brann and a new chapter," said Kaminski.

"There's only two levels in England that are professional. I definitely wanted to get European exposure, which I was never going to get in England.

"At the time, I was in discussions with a few clubs but it was things that I'd done before, or the project wasn't matching.

"I knew that when I came to Brann, I was going to coach top-level players. I wanted to be at the top of the competition and I was desperate to win a trophy."

Kaminski has urged other female coaches in England to go abroad and gain experience as she believes opportunities are too few in the WSL.

A study from UK Coaching in October showed there has been a 6% decline in the overall number of female coaches in recent years.

There are currently three English female coaches in the WSL - Jo Potter at Crystal Palace, Amy Merricks at Birmingham City and Karen Hills at Charlton Athletic - and they all came up with promoted clubs this summer.

But Kaminski says she is "concerned" about where they might go next and hopes more opportunities in English men's football will open up soon.

"I ended up leaving the country to go and get what I thought I deserved and had earned the right to work in, in terms of the level," said Kaminski.

"There's more than one female out there that's capable [of working in men's football]. I don't think it's out of reach. I would always, certainly, be open to it.

"At the moment, for me, there's not enough consideration even for that opportunity to be given to female managers who are more than capable.

"I think the foundations are there for females to take the plunge but is the world of football ready? I'm unsure."

#767. Japan's Tashima to stand against Infantino for Fifa presidency

Kozo Tashima became president of the Japan Football Association in 2016

The Japan Football Association honorary president, Kozo Tashima, has announced his intention to stand against Gianni Infantino to be the next Fifa president.

Tashima, 68, is a member of the Fifa Council and a former international footballer and coach.

He said he wants to convey "integrity, soundness, and high moral standards" and "contribute to a better future for football".

Infantino has been under intense scrutiny since it emerged he had been planning to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

The Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal was abandoned at the end of July, after significant backlash from across world football.

The deadline for candidates to stand in the election is 18 November.

Whilst support for Infantino was severely impacted by the FFE scandal, he has shored up support in recent months.

Infantino told BBC Sport last month that he felt he had the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football as he bids for a fourth term in charge of Fifa.

His comments came after he was "fully endorsed" by the Asian Football Confederation - following a U-turn by its president Sheikh Salman.

Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put their name forward in October for next year's Fifa presidential election.

However, Tashima's emergence as a challenger - with the backing of the Japan Football Association (JFA) - will now test the strength of Infantino's supporter base.

As with all candidates, Tashima will require the backing of five Fifa member associations.

Infantino laughs off resignation questions

Announcing his intentions, Tashima said: "I believe it is important to clearly communicate to the world of football the integrity, soundness, and high moral standards that Japanese football has cherished and built up over the years.

"I have decided to run for Fifa presidential election in order to convey this philosophy to the world and contribute to a better future for football.

"I will take on this challenge with strong determination, making use of the experience I have cultivated so far, and contributing to the further development of world football."

Tsuneyasu Miyamoto, president of the JFA, said: "This decision is a major challenge to contribute to the further development of world football by utilising that experience and knowledge, and at the same time, we believe it will be an opportunity to show the world the ideals and attitudes that Japanese football has cherished."

#766. Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker

Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

To most Bayern Munich fans under the age of 40, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge was the club CEO who regularly spoke his mind. Fans with longer memories, or a better grasp of Bavarian football history, recall Rummenigge as one of the club's all-time great players. He was also the last Bayern man to win the Ballon d'Or — in 1981. The last Bundesliga player to win was Borussia Dortmund's Matthias Sammer, in 1996.

That long drought ended on Monday, with Harry Kane, born 12 years after Rummenigge's win, picking up the 2026 trophy at a ceremony held, as a one-off, in his native London.

"I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special,” he said on stage.

Not many people would have thought it, and maybe even I wouldn't have thought I'd be this far," Kane later told British sports streaming plaftorm DAZN.

Lamine Yamal, the prodigious Barcelona and Spain forward who won the Euros at 16, finished third. At the end of the 2025-26 season, on which the award is judged, Yamal won the World Cup with Spain as well as the La Liga title. Kylian Mbappe came in second.

Kane's 73 goals for club and country last season made for a strong case, and the Bundesliga's most expensive signing of all time has already racked up 156 goals in 159 games for the serial German champions. But it's not just the numbers that tell the story, according to his club coach.

"People in England saw him as a goalscorer during his time playing there," Vincent Kompany said of Kane last season. "We've seen other qualities too, such as his footballing intelligence. We can appreciate that now — it was perhaps somewhat underestimated in England. He's like a fine wine that improves with age. I also enjoy that aspect of his game."

Kane continues to improve at 33, a point when many footballers start to regress. Though he is helped by being more reliant on guile and technique than pace, Kane's professionalism is key to staying at the top, according to his Bayern teammate Serge Gnabry.

"He always has the right attitude, always leads the way and sets the tone," Gnabry said ahead of Bayern's 2-2 draw in the Champions League against Arsenal last week. "He never strays from his path, helps the team with his performance and is a top-tier player."

Kane scored a penalty in that match and provided a sensational pass from which Alphonso Davies scored Bayern's opener, another reminder of his all-round game. "The pass was one of my best ones," Kane said after the match. "I knew Phonzy [Davies] would be able to get there with his speed. Whatever I can do to help the team, I'll do. At the moment, it seems to be with assists more than goals."

That attitude has been with Kane from the start. His first-ever coach, Dave Bricknell, from Ridgeway Rovers, an amateur club in northeast London, told DW after Kane joined Bayern from Spurs in 2023: "Harry's mentality is his greatest strength. He doesn't let anything worry him. If he misses a chance, he doesn't care — he will go and score from another chance."

His England coach, Thomas Tuchel, has also emphasized Kane's leadership. "He is the first one to push everyone, and that is his mindset, and he became a very, very hardworking forward on top of his finishing skills, Tuchel said in September as Kane extended his England goal-scoring record against the Czech Republic. "He is a complete package."

There are detractors who point to perceived "stat-padding," or scoring against inferior opponents in international qualifiers and in the Bundesliga, where there are fewer elite teams and a lot less money, than in England. Though Kane's ratio of 213 goals in 320 games in the Premier League is a little off his Bundesliga stats, it bears comparison with any other player in the history of the league.

Kane winning the award is also a boost in profile for the Bundesliga, which has been unable to keep pace, both commercially and on the pitch, with other top European leagues of late, particularly the Premier League and La Liga.

Winning it in a league outside of England or Spain perhaps makes Kane's feat even greater. Other than Ousmane Dembele, who won it last year after Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League win, and Lionel Messi, a serial Ballon d'Or winner, the last player to take the Ballon d'Or for a season played outside England or Spain was was Kaka at AC Milan in 2007, when Italy's Serie A was considered a stronger league.

Kane's career hasn't been straightforward, something he admitted in his speech. After signing his first senior contract with Spurs in July 2010, he was sent out on various loans to lower league sides between 2011-2013 without ever making a huge impression.

"My journey wasn't straightforward. I wasn't the kid who went straight to the top. I had to experience the downs, I had a lot of loan moves, I had to fight my way to be the very best right now, and I hope that can give you determination as well," Kane said in his speech.

For former teammate Jermain Defoe, who also coached Kane at Spurs, those experiences were formative.

"You have to show a resilience. It's not easy when you go out on loan, it can feel like you're being rejected by the club that you are at, which isn't the case," he told DW in 2023, before adding that Kane's ability was always clear.

"When he joined up with the [Tottenham] first team, you could see the potential," Defoe said. "He was always a good finisher, always hit the ball clean. … With Harry you already knew, he had that natural instinct and always felt comfortable in front of goal."

Those goals have, after a failure to win a trophy in England, led to two Bundesliga titles and a German Cup. But success with England remains elusive after a 2026 World Cup exit in the semifinals. Kane will be 35 by the time of the next Euros, in the UK and Ireland in 2028, and has a deal with Bayern until the following year. His form since joining Bayern suggests that he could get better still.

This article was first published on October 22, 2026. It was updated on October 27 after Harry Kane won the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

#765. New Met Gala 2027 Theme Revealed After John Galliano Controversy

After John Galliano dropped out of Met Gala 2027 amid controversy, The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced a new theme: “extraORDINARY: Fashion and the Poetics of the Everyday."

The first Monday in May will look a bit different this year.

That's because the 2027 Met Gala has unveiled a more casual theme.

Months after John Galliano withdrew from the event amid growing controversy, The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced a new spring 2027 Costume Institute exhibition—"extraORDINARY: Fashion and the Poetics of the Everyday"—put together by Curator in Charge Andrew Bolton, Stephanie Kramer and Emily Mushaben.

"I didn’t have a plan B," Bolton shared with Vogue Nov. 5. "It was really important to come up with an exhibition that wasn’t just a masterwork show or something that we could do a little bit more easily."

The theme will ask those in attendance Met Gala on May 3 to lean into the elevated everyday attire: T-shirts, jeans and sweatshirts.

"I wanted it to be as challenging and as provocative and as beautiful as a John show would have been," Bolton continued. "That was really important to me: to come up with an idea that wasn’t a substitute. And it had to have some sort of contemporary resonance.”

Following the Met Gala on May 3, the extraORDINARY exhibition will open to the public from May 9, 2027, through January 9, 2028.

Bolton's announcement comes two months after Galliano stepped away from the Met Gala, which was planning to honor his work, due to ongoing backlash over his past antisemitic comments.

"After much reflection and discussion with The Met and all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time," Galliano shared in an Aug. 31 Instagram message. "I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry for it."

"I understand that meaningful atonement is not achieved through an exhibition, institutional recognition or a single public gesture," he added. "It is a continuing responsibility, demonstrated through listening, learning and one's conduct over time."

Following Galliano's announcement, Vogue's Anna Wintour addressed the fashion designer's departure.

"I believe this is the right decision, and both he and the Museum have my full support," Wintour said. "His soaring imagination, fed by a lifetime of curiosity and research, is matched by his exceptional craft. Cut, fit, the evocative line of a bias-cut dress, color—he's a master of it all. Without one or the other, if his technique wasn't equal to his storytelling talents, he wouldn't be the premier couturier of his generation. But he most certainly is."

"The way that Christian Dior called Cristobal Balenciaga 'the master of us all,' a generation of designers have looked to Galliano as the greatest," she added. "His impact reverberates across generations, not least of all with Dior's current creative director Jonathan Anderson, who calls Galliano one of his heroes."

As prep for the 2027 Met Gala continues, keep reading for all the behind-the-scenes secrets of the star-studded event.

If you're lucky enough to score an invite to fashion's biggest event of the year, a solo ticket costs $30,000, while a table is yours for $275,000.

Fortunately, not everyone has to pay to attend, as Anna Wintour is known to invite up-and-coming designers to the gala. And, usually, the celebrities invited specifically to model a designer's work on the carpet don't have to pony up either.

And the steep price tag isn't enough to deter the rest of the stylish set: There is actually a waitlist.

"I've known of society names who couldn't get a ticket and are prepped to go if there's a last-minute seat that becomes available," vintage store owner Cameron Silver, who has attended the event several times, revealed to Page Six in 2017. "They have their look ready even if they aren't certain of whether they will actually have a seat days before the event."

It varies, with 500 being considered small and cozy and 800, the largest number of attendees the Met Gala has ever entertained, being deemed too big.

"We do want the experience to feel intimate for our guests," Vogue's Sylvana Ward Durrett told Fast Company in 2017, "so in the past few years, we've really scaled back and dropped numbers by almost 200 or 300 people." .

Despite its reputation for opulence and glam, the organizers actually want the event to feel exclusive for the lucky few who get to attend, with Wintour usually starting the list with the hopes of keeping it at 500. "We want to keep this an intimate setting because that's why people come to this," Ward Durrett is overheard saying in The First Monday in May.

And just because a celebrity is invited doesn't mean they automatically get a plus-one for their significant other; their partner must also land an invite of their own.

There's no rest for the fashionable as plans for the event usually start on the Tuesday immediately after the first Monday in May. (FYI, about 100 people work on the event year-round, including 10 full-time Vogue employees.)

"I'm a big fan of a one-sheet," Vogue's then-director of special projects Ward Durrett explained of her process. "We have sort of a running to-do list that just gets longer and longer as we get closer—and we literally go through [it] every day, even if it's redundant."

The first bullet point on her list? The tent. "Then you [write out] everything that's involved surrounding [that aspect]." Making this list helps her to think about the event "from start to finish—and to make sure that we're not missing anything."

As for how involved Wintour is with the details, the late Vogue contributing editor Andre Leon Talley said in The First Monday in May, "Anna is meticulously vetting every single thing, from the napkins to the forks to the lighting. The detail of the flowers, the detail of the ushers, how they're dressed, everything has been vetted for months and weeks and months and weeks."

And she prefers to keep the details close to her iconic Chanel dress, with Vogue contributing editor Plum Sykes telling The New York Post, "It's very secretive. [Wintour] doesn't want anyone to know what she's planning or what she's up to until the minute they walk down that red carpet and through the door."

If you've ever tried to do seating arrangements for a wedding, you might have a tiny understanding of just how difficult it is to do the seating chart for the Met Gala. This is one of the most important aspects of the event that the team spends the most time on, strategically seating guests by looking at common interests.

"A lot of thought goes into who sits next to who, if they sat together last year, if they've sat next to each other at other events, so much goes into it, it's shocking," Ward Durrett said in The First Monday in May. "A lot of power-brokering."

Of course, each year the seating arrangements go through many, many changes as the event takes shape, with Ward Durett telling Vogue she learned early on to invest in Velcro over post-it notes to avoid any errors. "There have been many iterations of the seating chart," she said. "When I first started, we had just little stickies, and it was a nightmare—things were falling off, we were losing people and rewriting names a million times a day."

Color-coding is also used, as Ward Durrett likes to go with the woman-man-woman-man pattern if possible. And another key rule that might surprise you: "Never seat spouses next to each other," she said. "The whole point of these things is to meet new people, and to be interested in what others are doing. What's the point if you come here to hang out with your husband?" Sorry, Blake Lively and Ryan Reynolds!

Listen, every event has that table that gets the nosebleed seats, usually near the kitchen and/or the bathroom. The Met Gala is no exception, so designers' table positions usually change each year.

And Wintour is very involved in the process, infamously chastising her team for trying to hide the H&M table in a scene from The First Monday in May. "We shouldn't bury this table," she said, "seriously, that's not fair."

Though it's not a luxury brand or atelier, H&M (also an advertiser in Vogue and other publications) and more accessible brands such as Topshop and Zara have started having more of a presence on fashion's biggest night. Making its debut in 2015, H&M scored a big win by having Sarah Jessica Parker wear a custom gown.

Given that it is one of the most A-list events, it's impossible not to have Hollywood exes and frenemies seated near each other. Remember when Selena Gomez and The Weeknd attended along with his ex Bella Hadid? So it's likely taken into consideration that, say, Taylor Swift and Katy Perry shouldn't have been at the same table at the height of their feud. But, ultimately, the overall event trumps any potential tension among the attendees.

"You can't please everybody. We always like to think there's not a bad [seat] in the house, which really there isn't. You have to come away confident in the notion that you are doing your best, and that inevitably not everyone will be happy," Ward Durrett said. "But we have a pretty good track record. The instances are few and far between, and we always try and work more closely with them the next year to manage expectations."

(In one memorable scene in the First Monday in May, Ward Durrett had placed three Velcro tabs to the side of her seating chart, bluntly telling Wintour, "Those are people I am hoping will go away.")

Alas, not everyone is happy with their assigned seat, as fashion critic Cathy Horn noted in her 2006 piece for The New York Times: "John Lydon, the former Sex Pistol known as Johnny Rotten, found his seat—the last at a long table and arguably one of the least desirable in the highly orchestrated seating plan—he was visibly upset...[he] stormed out twice, cursing museum workers."

During a 2018 appearance on The Late Late Show, James Corden asked Wintour to name any celebrity she would never invite back to the Met Gala.

"Donald Trump," she responded. (President Trump and wife Melania Trump have attended the Met Gala several times over the years, though they last climbed those infamous stairs in 2012.)

Another celeb who claims to have been banned from the Met Gala? Former Project Runway mentor Tim Gunn, who alleged he was blacklisted by Wintour after telling a story about her to The Post that she found unflattering.

"All hell broke loose, it was insane," he said on E!'s Fashion Police back in 2016. "So we have had an open war ever since."

And while Billy Porter didn't claim he was persona non grata, he hasn't struck a pose at the event since his 2019 debut.

"Last year was Black dandyism and I was not invited, I’m just going to throw that out there," he noted on an April 2026 episode of SiriusXM’s Bevelations. "The reality is when people ask me, you need to know I was not invited and I don’t go to places where I’m not welcome."

Yes, dinner is actually served at the event, with Stephen Colbert once revealing all of the guests had to wait for Wintour to take her seat before digging in.

And, like every other aspect, Wintour is heavily involved in the menu planning for each gala.

A Vogue employee told The Post that Wintour once banned ingredients that had the potential to get stuck in your teeth (parsley) or could give a guest bad breath (a lot of garlic) or, worst of all, stain their gown. So appetizers are made to be easily eaten.

Wintour usually prefers that the food served somewhat correspond to the theme. Though that doesn't always work out.

Glorious Food owner Sean Driscoll, who catered every Met Gala from 1995 through 2018, said the decision to serve lamb potpies for 2011's "Alexander McQueen: Savage Beauty" theme resulted in "a lot of special requests" as "many [guests] did not want to eat that."

But they also want the food to look good, with The First Monday in May director Andrew Rossi admitting he was shocked by the level of detail, especially when he attended a tasting with Wintour and watched her: "We see Anna literally going on her phone to look up the presentations of different food."

No one is exactly sure why the mandate was instated, as no official explanation has ever been given for the decision to ban selfies and the use of social media from the glamorous and already-FOMO-inducing event. But it was made by Wintour in 2015.

At the time, a Vogue source revealed to Pret-a-Reporter that a notice went out to all invitees, warning, "The use of phones for photography and social media will not be permitted inside the gala."

The magazine declined to comment on the report, but a source told The Hollywood Reporter at the time, "It has solely to do with guests' security and enjoyment of the event."

Wintour's disdain for phones at the event was clear in a memorable scene from The First Monday in May, wherein she discovered a male celebrity—whose name had been blurred, per Wintour's request—decided to attend the event after initially declining. "Can he not be on his cell phone the entire time then?" she asked Ward Durrett.

In an interview with The Post, Ward Durrett explained, "Anna is sort of an old-school traditionalist. She likes a dinner party where people are actually speaking to each other. We aren't sitting over people's shoulders, but if it's an obvious thing we might gently remind them."

Still, despite Wintour's ban, snap-happy celebs have broken the rule many times, including Kylie Jenner's infamous bathroom selfie from the 2017 affair.

Technically, you must be 18 years or older to attend the big event, with organizers confirming the age restriction ahead of the 2018 Met Gala after Maddie Ziegler revealed she was unable to attend because she was only 15. "I can't go, because I'm not old enough!" she told The Hollywood Reporter.

"It's not an appropriate event for people under 18," the event's organizer explained to THR, with the new age limit going into effect that year.

Prior to 2018, some of the youngest guests included siblings Jaden Smith and Willow Smith attending in 2016 when they were 17 and 15, respectively, Elle Fanning making her debut when she was just 13, and Hailee Steinfeld attending her first Met Gala in 2011 at age 14.

But there seems to be a loophole for the younger fashionistas in Hollywood: A minor may tag along if their parents are in attendance.

While Wintour has final say over every attendee's attire, their looks technically do not have to be approved by the Vogue global editorial director (though she is aware of everything that gets to walk the famous carpet).

"Each celebrity has been chosen to wear a gown by a designer. It's like assignments," Andre Leon Talley said in The First Monday in May, with former Givenchy creative director Riccardo Tisci, who dressed Beyoncé and Madonna for the 2016 Met Gala, further explaining, "Each designer brings his own muse. You bring a person that most represents your aesthetic."

That means that, for the most part, a celebrity's look is up to the designer that invited them.

While each year's gala has a theme—2024's was "Sleeping Beauties: Reawakening Fashion", 2019's was "Camp: Notes on Fashion"—there are no strict guidelines when it comes to a guest or designer's interpretation.

But how is the theme actually selected? It's a long process that starts well over a year before the first Monday of May, with Andrew Bolton, the tireless longtime curator of The Costume Institute at New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art, choosing something that is culturally relevant.

"What I try to do is work on a topic that seems timely, and that defines a cultural shift that's happening or is about to happen," he explained to Vogue. "We always try to have a menu of shows that are dynamic, that go back and forth on subjects from the past and the present, between thematic shows and monographic ones of a single designer. We try to mix it up."

After he narrows down his search, he presents it for approval to the museum's director before Wintour then signs off on it about one year ahead of time.

"It would be difficult to do it without her support," the esteemed British curator explained. "Anna works out what sponsors would be appropriate for the exhibition. Sometimes I have an idea, and it's less of a big idea or popular idea, which is not terribly appealing to sponsors."

Once the guests have walked the red carpet and survived the iconic steps, they then greet Wintour and the other hosts (2026 co-chairs include Beyoncé, Nicole Kidman and Venus Williams) in a receiving line, which generally takes quite a bit of time with all the air kissing and exchanging of pleasantries.

After that, they are invited to walk through The Costume Institute's exhibition before it opens to the public. Then it's time to eat, mingle and network, with music, dancing and performances from the likes Rihanna and Lady Gaga.

Speaking of the high-profile performers, a lot of the stress in terms of planning the Met Gala stems from the entertainment aspect of the night.

As infamously documented in The First Monday in May, Ward Durrett faced a major budgetary issue when it came to booking Rihanna for that year's gala.

"It's about twice as much as any performer we've ever had," she said of Rihanna's undisclosed fee after having a conversation on the phone with someone from the superstar's team. "They're not interested in making it come down any further."

Eventually, Wintour was called to step in and figure out the situation.

Celebrities are allowed to bring their own security guards to the event, in addition to the ones hired by the Museum for the red carpet.

But really, the objects that require the most security detail are the jewels. One year, Lively wore $3.5 million worth of baubles, while Karlie Kloss was once draped in $2.5 million worth of Forevermark jewels for the event.

"The full security process is kept top secret because of the incredibly high value of the pieces involved, but there is always a security guard present until the pieces are safely returned," a Forevermark rep told E! News. Additional security measures are also taken, like RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) trackers and video monitoring.

So yes, Ocean's 8 definitely got that aspect of the Met Gala right.

Given that many dresses are custom-made for the Met Gala or are pulled from designer's couture archives, it's rare that celebrities are allowed to keep their gowns. More often than not, they go back to the design house to be archived.

Though, in 2018, Balmain's Olivier Rousteing teamed up with Bono's RED to auction off custom pieces worn by celebs such as Jennifer Lopez, Alex Rodriguez, Trevor Noah, with 100 percent of the proceeds going toward the foundation's Global Fund.

For 2021's event, attendees were required to wear face masks and provide proof of their COVID-19 vaccination, which led to rapper Nicki Minaj choosing not to partake in the fashionable festivities.

"They want you to get vaccinated for the Met," Minaj posted on Twitter. "if I get vaccinated it won't [be] for the Met. It'll be once I feel I've done enough research. I'm working on that now. In the meantime my loves, be safe. Wear the mask with 2 strings that grips your head & face. Not that loose one."

#764. Emery close to agreeing new Aston Villa contract

Unai Emery has been Aston Villa manager since October 2022

Aston Villa head coach Unai Emery is close to agreeing a contract extension at the club - which will hand him even more responsibility for long-term development.

The Villa boss held talks with the hierarchy on Wednesday to discuss the club's future, with all parties keen on extending his time at Villa Park.

Emery would relish the opportunity to play an even bigger role in developing the club for the long term, with talks ongoing about the fine details, the finances, and the length of the new deal.

The plan is to announce the new contract once all details have been agreed, which is unlikely to be before the weekend.

Emery, whose team won the Europa League in May â Villa's first major trophy in 30 years â celebrated four years at the club last month.

In his time at Villa he has transformed the side, from a group who were in a relegation fight to one who have qualified for European football every season under his management.

The Spaniard has been linked with a move to Manchester United, who Villa play this weekend at Old Trafford, should they sack boss Michael Carrick.

Emery, though, who was already under contract until 2029, is now close to signing a new longer-term deal.

On Wednesday night, Villa released a statement saying a meeting had taken place between Emery, club chairman Nassef Sawiris, executives Roberto Olabe and Damian Vidagany.

The club said: "The discussions focused on jointly planning the club's long-term strategic direction, with positive discussions establishing a clear commitment beyond 2029 for the joint development of the club under the sporting leadership of Unai Emery based on the shared ambitions and common goal to reach excellency and keep growing during the next years.

"The objective is clear: to build an ambitious, competitive Aston Villa capable of taking on the biggest challenges and achievements."

Emery, a former Arsenal, Sevilla and Paris St-Germain boss, joined Villa in 2022 from Villarreal.

After a tumultuous summer in which the spine of Emery's side that finished fourth in the Premier League and lifted European silverware was sold, Villa are currently 10th in the Premier League and have won three of their four opening matches in the Champions League.

Villa threatened pundit and former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher with legal action last month after he suggested Emery would be a good choice if Manchester United were looking for a new manager, with Carragher also telling fans of the club to "shut up". However, Villa dropped the threat after he apologised.

#763. The oracle of the second quadrant

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Chao Liu has driven up and down the US East Coast — from Florida to Massachusetts — before detouring to France. His latest stop is at IFREMER, where he will continue to pretend to be a real scientist until someone finally catches on.

The machine sat between the deep-fryer truck and a three-legged goat, housed inside a canvas tent that smelled heavily of kerosene and stale popcorn. It was a massive, rivet-popped iron boiler known officially as the Differential Analytical Oscillator, although the hand-painted sign out front simply read: THE DAO BOILER — KNOWS ALL, TELLS ALL. FIVE CENTS.

By late afternoon, the fairground was a soup of churned mud and diesel exhaust.

“It don’t do lottery numbers,” the operator said, not looking up from the greasy carburettor he was scraping with a butter knife. He was a small, sour man named Silas, wearing a leather apron stiff with soot. “And if you’re gonna ask if your brother’s a bastard, save your nickel. The answer is always yes.”

Jerry shifted his boots in the sawdust. He was 19, wore a stained canvas jacket, and had spent the past three days trying to look tragically heartbroken on his front porch. “I don’t care about the lottery. I want to know about Clara.”

Silas sighed, spitting a dark stream of tobacco juice into a bucket of scrap iron. “The butcher’s girl? She left on the 4.10 rail to Lowmarsh. What’s to know? She wanted indoor plumbing and a man who didn’t smell like fertilizer.”

“No,” Jerry said, his jaw tightening as he dropped a heavy brass nickel onto the tool chest. “She said it wasn’t that. She said there was a … a fundamental misalignment in our vectors. I want to know what that means. I want the real, exact reason.”

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures

Silas looked at the coin, then at Jerry’s face. He let out a dry, rattling chuckle. “The exact reason? All right, kid. But the tub don’t do poetry. You want the low-voltage ribbon or the full squeeze?”

“Give me the whole thing,” Jerry said, crossing his arms. “Don’t spare the details.”

Silas shrugged, picking up a heavy, lead-lined copper helmet attached to the boiler by a thick bundle of rubber-coated cables. It looked like an old diving apparatus, dripping with mineral oil. “Put it on. Full throttle means you get the absolute breakdown. Don’t say I didn’t warn you.”

Jerry lifted the helmet. It was incredibly heavy, cold against his ears. He lowered it over his head, plunging himself into absolute darkness.

For three seconds, there was only the smell of hot grease and the rhythmic thump-thump-thump of the internal pistons. Then, the engine engaged the clutch.

The Universe didn’t open up with grand spiritual enlightenment. It opened with a relentless, deafening avalanche of raw data.

Jerry didn’t see Clara’s face, or a vision of her on the train. Instead, a cold, mechanical voice began reading a molecular ledger directly into his auditory cortex. It informed him that on Tuesday at 3.14 p.m., the atmospheric humidity had caused a 0.04% swelling in the leather of Clara’s left boot, which altered her gait by three millimetres. This structural variance, combined with the gravitational pull of a passing manure spreader, had shifted her centre of gravity exactly enough to cause a microscopic tear in the cotton fibre of her socks.

The machine kept going. It explained that the chemical composition of Jerry’s afternoon sweat contained an excess of sulfur molecules that reacted poorly with the zinc coating on his porch railing, creating a localized scent profile that her olfactory nerves categorized under Sub-Class 4: Decaying Organic Matter. It gave him the exact thermodynamic equation of the breeze that had carried the smell to her nose. It gave him the precise atomic mass of the dust particle she choked on when she tried to say goodbye.

It went on for what felt like an eternity, resolving her ‘broken heart’ into a massive, agonizingly boring list of friction coefficients, cellular degeneration rates and barometric pressure shifts. There was no love. There was no betrayal. There was only a three-hour maths problem about why a girl walked towards a train station.

The helmet was violently yanked off his head.

Jerry stumbled backwards, blinking against the harsh light of the tent. The machine was smoking, its violet glow dying back into a dull, rusted grey. Silas was standing over him, holding the helmet, looking thoroughly bored.

#762. Nicholas Hoult, Wife Bryana Holly Privately Welcome Twins

Nicholas Hoult confirmed that he and Bryana Holly are now parents to four kids, with his How To Rob A Bank costar Pete Davidson revealing that the couple welcomed twins while filming the upcoming movi

Nicholas Hoult and Bryana Holly know how to privately expand their family.

The Warm Bodies actor and his longtime partner are now the parents of four, his How To Rob A Bank costar Pete Davidson confirmed in a recent interview alongside Hoult.

“He’s a great dad,” Davidson said during an interview with Entertainment Tonight, which also included Anna Sawai. “Father of four. Four under 7.”

And when Davidson—who welcomed his daughter Scottie in December 2025 with ex Elsie Hewitt—nodded toward Hoult to confirm, the 36-year-old confirmed, “Yeah.”

“Which is nuts,” the Saturday Night Live star continued. “Elsie was pregnant while we were filming and he had just had his twins and he would fly back every weekend to go see his family and that was really awesome.”

E! News has reached out to reps for Hoult and Holly regarding his latest comment but has not yet heard back.

While Hoult did not say much about welcoming twins with Holly—with whom he also shares son Joaquin, 7, and another child born in 2022—he is notoriously private about his inner world.

In fact, when the couple—who started dating in 2016—sparked speculation they had welcomed another baby following their appearance at the Oscars 2026 in March, Hoult stayed out of the conversation.

However, not everyone stayed so quiet. Responding to a user noting that Holly’s “surgeon did an amazing job,” regarding her appearance at the Vanity Fair Oscars afterparty, the fashion brand Lurelly—who designed Holly’s look—responded from its official account, “If by surgeon you mean her newborn baby. I can’t wait for a world where we root for each other rather than assume.”

Lurelly added of Holly’s appearance that “some people are naturally blessed,” with the original commenter writing back that they “would have never known she just had a baby.”

For Holly’s part, she appeared to subtly confirm that she and Hoult had welcomed more than just one baby in a separate post slamming the speculation on her breast size.

“I am seeing the comments around my chest and not that *anyone* is owed an explanation,” she wrote on Instagram Stories March 17, “but this is the product of a breast feeding mother who hasn’t fed her babies in hours ok!”

Not wholly confirming she was a mother of four, Holly added, “If you know, then you know.”

For a look into what Hoult and Holly have shared about their romance, keep reading…

Nicholas Hoult first met Bryana Holly while in California, The Favourite actor told the Evening Standard in January 2019. Although he’s kept mum on the details of their romance, the model shared a loving tribute for their 7th anniversary in 2023 featuring snaps of them from over the years.

The Great star previously shared insight into how his upbringing ultimately shaped aspects of his relationship with Bryana, including smaller moments like sharing a space together.

“I don’t feel as though I’m that possessive over things like that,” Nicholas told The Journal in November 2017. “She can put her stuff wherever she likes. My dad was an air pilot so he was flying a lot, and I grew up with my two sisters and my mum so I was used to ‘girl things’ being around and a ‘girl environment’ in the household.”

Nicholas and Bryana privately welcomed their first baby, a son named Joaquin, in 2018. While he’s largely grown up out of the public eye, he made his first public appearance in March 2024 while attending an Atlanta Hawks home game alongside his dad.

The Skins alum has given glimpses into his life as a dad and the learning curve that comes with it.

"There's a lot to take in," he told James Corden on The Late Late Show in May 2020. "But overall, it's like that time again, it brings back a lot of memories of your childhood. It makes you play again—which I'm really enjoying."

Nicholas and Bryana welcomed another baby, whose name they have not publicly shared, in 2022.

The couple have stepped out for a rare date night over the years, including a courtside outing at a game between the Los Angeles Lakers and the Philadelphia 76ers in 2023 and a stylish trip to Paris Fashion Week.

In a November 2026 interview, Hoult appeared to confirm that he and his wife had welcomed twins, agreeing as his How To Rob a Bank costar Pete Davidson detailed his life as a dad.

"He had just had his twins," Davidson explained of Hoult's dynamic while filming, "and he would fly back every weekend to go see his family and that was really awesome.”

#760. Russell Brand Found Guilty of Rape, 3 Counts of Sexual Assault

Russell Brand has been convicted of rape and multiple counts of sexual assault over a year after his legal battle began in London.

Russell Brand’s legal battle has reached a conclusion.

On Nov. 5, a London court found the 51-year-old was convicted on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

After deliberating for over eight hours, according to multiple outlets, the jury found Brand guilty of raping a fan in 2009 after meeting at one of his shows in London, of groping an MTV worker in 2004, kissing and groping another woman at her workplace in 2009 and of sexually assaulting another woman in 2009.

Brand—who had pleaded not guilty to all charges—was cleared of two separate counts of rape and one count of indecent assault.

The presiding judge Joel Bennathan, according to The New York Times, said he would sentence the Forgetting Sarah Marshall actor to “significant custodial time,” while also denying him bail.

British sentencing guidelines for rape, per the outlet, carry a maximum sentence of life in prison, while the average prison term for such a conviction is four to 19 years.

Brand’s legal battle began in April 2025, when he was charged with one count of rape, one count of oral rape, two counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault by the London Metropolitan Police. The events in question allegedly occurred between 1999 and 2009.

In December 2025, the actor was also charged with one additional count of rape and one more sexual assault charge, the London Metropolitan Police confirmed in a press release.

At the time, Brand—father to three with wife Laura Brand—shared a video to social media urging viewers “to understand the truth of my situation and scenario,” though he didn’t address the allegations directly.

“I pray Lord, anyone that I’ve harmed or hurt in my years of mindlessness and sin would be healed, Lord,” he said in the clip. “And I pray, Lord, for the absolute truth of who I am to be abundantly revealed.”

Despite the convictions, however, Brand’s legal journey may not be done.

According to the New York Times, citing an emailed statement following the verdicts, a spokeswoman for the Metropolitan Police said police had questioned Brand about two additional accusations of rape, submitting the files to prosecutors.

During the trial, per the outlet, Brand did not deny that some of the encounters had occurred, though he claimed every act had been consensual.

He reportedly told jurors, per the NYT, that while he “misused” his fame to obtain sexual encounters, he had always obtained consent, saying doing so had been “fundamental, essential, necessary.”

E! News has reached out to Brand’s legal team for comment but has not yet heard back.

Following Brand’s conviction, Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy released a statement praising the verdict.

“As his profile grew, so too did his sense of entitlement,” Furphy said, per CNN. “I hope this conviction sends a clear message that no one is above the law, no matter how famous or powerful they may be.”

#758. Beverly Hills, 90210 Actress Kimmarie Johnson Dead at 50

Kimmarie Johnson, who starred in Beverly Hills 90210 and Dude, Where’s My Car? has died after suffering heart issues, her niece told TMZ. She was 50.

The sun has set too soon on the life of another beloved Beverly Hills, 90210 star.

Kimmarie Johnson, who portrayed Judy in multiple episodes of the teen drama, died following a “heart event,” her niece Rhonda Scott told TMZ Nov. 5. She was 50.

Johnson, per TMZ, experienced the medical emergency on Oct. 27 at her home in Los Angeles before being rushed to Cedars-Sinai Hospital. There, she was diagnosed with a “heart aneurysm condition,” per the outlet. She died Nov. 4 after her heart stopped beating.

After a small role in Let’s Talk About Sex, Johnson made her debut on Beverly Hills, 90210 in 1998, working alongside the likes of Jennie Garth, Tori Spelling and Brian Austin Green.

She later went on to have small roles in projects such as Dude, Where’s My Car? alongside Austin Kutcher and Jennifer Garner in 2000, in addition to other film roles through 2017, when she made her last on-screen appearance as Rebekah in Tucker’s War.

Aside from her acting career, Johnson founded her own skincare consulting company, Skin Glow, in 2011 and modeled for print campaigns and runway shows. In 1993, she won the Miss Pennsylvania USA Beauty Pageant and went on to be a finalist in the Miss USA competition.

Born in Pittsburgh, Johnson graduated from Wilkinsburg High School in 1985. She went on to study at California University in Pennsylvania, before moving to New York City and then Los Angeles to pursue. a career in modeling.

Johnson is survived by her niece, as well as her son Cameron Nino, who was born in 2003.

Johnson’s passing comes after Beverly Hills, 90210 has had a difficult few years of loss, with Shannen Doherty dying in 2024 following a yearslong battle with breast cancer and David Gail dying the same year from cardiac arrest.

Following Doherty’s death, Garth—who acknowledged she and Doherty were “pitted against each other” on Beverly Hills—called her “courageous, passionate, determined and very loving and generous.”

“Our connection was real and honest,” Garth wrote in a tribute at the time. “I will miss her and will always honor her deeply in my heart and in my memories.”

To revisit memories from Beverly Hills, keep reading…

Created by Darren Star, the show was originally called Class of Beverly Hills, and at one point, Star, who based the show loosely on his own high school experience in Potomac, Md., used the working title Potomac 20854 before its now-iconic title was settled on.

While Beverly Hills, 90210 would go on to become one of the most popular TV shows of the '90s and be largely responsible for launching the teen soap genre, the Fox show was a dud when it first debuted in 1990, ranking No. 118 in the ratings (going up against NBC's Cheers didn't help).

But after the season one finale, featuring Brenda and Dylan's first time, started gaining buzz, Fox smartly ordered new episodes for the summer, providing some much-needed teen angst and drama in what used to be the TV off-season.

"We filmed all of our risqué summer episodes at the beach and aired those at the time when the other shows were in reruns," Jennie Garth told the New York Times. "So we caught a huge teen audience, kids that were home from school. And then it just went crazy."

From there, 90210 went from low-rated guilty pleasure to cultural phenomenon and the mostly unknown stars became some of the most famous people in the world.

"In just a matter of weeks, we went from being just another generic ensemble cast of any old prime-time drama to being…superstars," Garth wrote in her memoir. "I don't think any of us were prepared for the stardom that was thrust upon us in this way."

Before being cast as one of TV's ultimate heartthrobs, Luke Perry was working construction as a way to pay his bills between auditions—including for the role of Steve Sanders, which ultimately went to Ian Ziering.

But when producers realized they were lacking a brooding bad boy, Perry, then 27, got the call. "When Luke walked into the audition, it was like 'Wow, that's the person,'" Star gushed to Rolling Stone. "He seems exactly like James Dean to me, but it isn't a conscious imitation—he's really being himself."

Dylan McKay was initially only going to appear in a few episodes, but it was clear from the moment he drove up in that black Porsche 356 Speedster that a star was born—though Spelling had to fight to make Perry a series regular. (Imagine their reaction when they learned 20 people were injured after a riot broke out at a mall during one of Perry's appearances when 10,000 fans showed up?)

Perry remained on the show until 1995, leaving for three years to pursue other opportunities before returning in 1998, and remained on until the end, often credited as a special guest star.

In March 2019, Perry died at the age of 52 after suffering a stroke. He was starring on Riverdale, the latest teen soap that can credit the original 90210 for leading the way, playing the father of Archie (KJ Apa), the show's brooding lead. While he wasn't set to appear on Fox's BH90210 revival that year, the show paid tribute to the beloved star in its premiere.

Fearful of nepotism, executive producer Aaron Spelling's daughter Tori Spelling auditioned under a fake name, Tori Mitchell (inspired by a character Heather Locklear played in a TV movie her dad produced), reading for the roles of Kelly and Andrea before landing the role of Donna Martin.

"I heard about the show from my agent. She said, 'Your dad is doing it.' I was like, 'I haven't heard anything about it,'" Spelling told EW. "I popped into his briefcase when he got home, and I was like, cool. I really wanted to play Andrea. I went in under a different name, then I got the part of Donna—which I'm sure had something to do with my dad."

Donna ended up the cener of many an iconic moment, including the infamous "Donna Martin graduates!" chant when getting drunk on prom night got her banned from the graduation ceremony. In his memoir, Jason Priestley revealed a prank he pulled on that day of filming: Knowing they were going to reloop the dialogue anyway, Priestley got the group of extras to chant "Donna Martin masturbates!" instead, finding the opportunity "pretty irresistible."

Shannen Doherty, previously known for the pitch-black high school comedy Heathers, was named the cast's Biggest Diva upon graduation from West Beverly, and Brenda Walsh only stayed through one season of 90210's college years.

"Her lateness was appalling, and she had a callous attitude and an indifference," former executive producer Charles Rosin told EW in 2000. Aaron Spelling added, "It wasn't like she ruined the show or anything. It just upset the cast members tremendously."

Doherty admitted, "There was definitely a time that I did not want to be there. I was unhappy."

The final straw for producers was rumored to be Doherty's decision to cut her hair in the middle of filming the season four finale in 1994, which saw Brenda deciding to move to London to pursue acting.

But later Spelling admitted going to her father to expedite Doherty's firing.

"I felt like I was a part of something, a movement, that cost someone their livelihood," an emotional Spelling said during a 2015 special. "Was she a horrible person? No. She was one of the best friends I ever had."

After Doherty's death at 53 in July 2024 following a years-long battle with breast cancer, all of her former costars paid tribute. Priestley called her a "force of nature," while Spelling remembered her as "a rebel in an era when most women didn’t feel comfortable being strong."

After Doherty's dramatic exit, the pressure was on to find her replacement.

"We obviously had an exhaustive search to replace her," executive producer Larry Mollin told TeenDramaW--re in 2010. "We looked at many people."

Alicia Silverstone, Alyssa Milano and Drew Barrymore were all reportedly in contention, but 90210 went with Saved By the Bell star Tiffani Amber-Thiessen, whose scheming Valerie Malone was the opposite of cheery Kelly Kapowski.

"We wanted a baaad girl. There was really an edge with Tiffani because she was so sexual," producer Rosin told EW. "In her first episode, she [smoked] some pot. We were making a statement there." (In her first scene, she memorably rolls a joint with one hand, though a stunt double was needed.)

Viewers responded immediately to the character, but there was one cast member who didn't love Thiessen: Brian Austin Green, her real-life boyfriend at the time.

"When we cast her, Brian was so upset! Oh my god, he felt betrayed!" Mollin recalled. "We were totally shocked and had no idea. But, then, of course, we realized why: because other people would be kissing...his girlfriend!"

Fact: If you assemble a cast of young, attractive, available people and have them work together for an extended period of time, they will hook up.

"Various combinations of people slept with each other over the years," Priestley shared in his memoir, undoubtedly filling fans with righteous joy that their suspicions were right all these years later. Priestley went on to say his "full-fledged adult relationship" was with Christine Elise (aka Emily Valentine), whom he dated for five years.

During a test on Celebrity Lie Detector, Spelling said she had a quick summer fling with Priestley, dated Green (saying she was "always in love" with her onscreen beau), and once kissed Perry. (Priestley's response? "I'm not getting into this... It's nobody's business... Either way...," he tweeted.)

After dating Thiessen for several years, Green started seeing Vanessa Marcil, who played one of David's non-Donna love interests, Gina Kincaid. They split up in 2003 and share now grown son Kassius.

If viewers thought the rivalry between Brenda and Kelly was intense, it was nothing compared to the behind-the-scenes feuding between Doherty and Garth, with Spelling often attempting (and failing) to play peacemaker.

"I don't know why it is, but there is a universal truth that when you put three teenage girls together, some serious s--t is going to go down," Garth wrote in her 2013 memoir, "even if it meant sounding like a complete and utter b---h. Poor Tori, the youngest of the three of us was, inevitably, often caught in the middle and she was always trying to smooth things over, trying to get Shan and me off each other's backs and get along, but her efforts usually failed."

Things got so heated that the two stars once came very close to throwing punches (with some accounts saying fists actually did fly), with Garth revealing the cause of the blowup (which the male cast members had to step in to de-escalate): Doherty pulled up Garth's skirt while filming a scene. Garth, describing the two of them as "gasoline and a match," wrote, "I did snap and I yelled at her, something to the effect of, 'Come on, b---h! We're talking this outside!'"

Fortunately, Doherty and Garth ultimately reconciled.

"Our connection was real and honest," Garth wrote on Instagram after Doherty's death. "We were so often pitted against each other but none of that reflected the truth of our real relationship which was one built on mutual respect and admiration."

It might be hard to believe, but back in the early '90s, 16-year-old Brenda losing her virginity to Dylan at the spring dance was a big effin' deal. And the biggest outcry came from scandalized local affiliates (or the people who wrote in to them to complain) who were upset that Brenda's first time was...perfectly fine!

"I was strongly advised to write a show that would address the consequences of that sexual experience," Star revealed to The New York Times. "So the first episode of the second season Brenda broke up with Dylan because their relationship had gotten too mature."

While Kelly Taylor was battling cults, cocaine use, love triangles and amnesia onscreen, Garth was privately struggling with anxiety from the age of 19, as she revealed in her memoir.

"I felt comfortable—almost comforted—by all of the workers buzzing around me during the day, but after hours, I'd find myself getting anxious when strangers approached me," she wrote. "And so simple tasks, like going to the grocery store, or the mall, or to get gas, became overwhelming exercises in having to be ‘on' when my natural inclination was to shut down and not interact with anyone. I…began to suffer a level of anxiety that as, at times, nearly paralyzing. When the panic attacks started to kick in, I became even more withdrawn."

She revealed at one point she had "stopped going to the movies or clothes shopping or doing any of the other things normal young people do," waiting until well after dark to step out of her home. "I wouldn't say that I ever stepped over the line into full-blown agoraphobia, but I would say I definitely came close."

While Ziering mostly avoided any and all drama on set, he revealed he had an emotional breakdown in season four after a storyline of Steve's was cut.

"There was an episode where Steve was accused of rape," he told HuffPost Live in 2015. "But, they edited out so much powerful stuff. That was like the first time I really got some great words to say and I work-shopped them and I studied. I brought game, and it never even made it through the edit."

Feeling "betrayed" by the producers' decision not to air the scenes without letting him know first, Ziering lost his cool.

"I tore the dressing rooms apart," he revealed. "We all work so hard for our characters and to not even get a heads up...I'm not a volatile person, I have a very long fuse, but after working so hard on this particular episode, I just didn't feel like they were with me on this one."

Jason Priestley's Partying and Parting Ways

After becoming a heartthrob as ultimate nice guy Brandon, Priestley was desperate to shed the goody-two-shoes image in real life, so he indulged in some hard partying "to prove that I was nothing like the sanctimonious Brandon Walsh," he wrote in his memoir. (During a 2014 Watch What Happens Live! appearance, Garth said he partied the hardest out of all the cast members.)

"When you're young like that, you feel like a hamster on a wheel. All you're doing is spinning that wheel and your world," he told The Hollywood Reporter. "You have a bunch of people telling you how great you are, so it's really easy to just start believing it after a while."

Priestley ended up changing his ways (thanks in large part to his relationship with costar Elise), going on to become a producer on the show and directing episodes, which is why Brandon's unceremonious exit in season nine hurt his feelings at the time.

"I did the first scene of the morning—literally with this actor who was brought in to replace me—and that was it. I hugged the crew, picked up my box of stuff, went to my car and drove away," he told the Guardian. "There was no party, no nothing. I felt like I'd wasted nine years of my life."

He returned in a video message—Brandon's well-wishes for Donna and David when they tied the knot—for the series finale in 2000.

After initially auditioning for Brenda, believing that being a twin IRL would give her an edge, Gabrielle Carteris landed the role of Andrea—after the 29-year-old lied about her age to snag the part of the academically minded 16-year-old. (Fun fact: Teen Witch star Robyn Lively, then Priestley's girlfriend, turned down the role of Andrea first.)

"I actually talked to a lawyer about how could I sign these contracts and lie about my age and still be able to do the show. Is it OK?" she told Access Hollywood. "[The lawyer said] ‘Yes it is, as long as you just say you're over 21.'"

A main cast member for the first five seasons, producers reluctantly worked Carteris' real-life pregnancy into the show, making Andrea pregnant and marrying her off to the baby's father, her boyfriend Jesse Vasquez (Mark Espinoza). But by the end of the fifth season, the producers felt Andrea's time in America's most famous zip code had run its course and sent her off to Yale with her young family.

"It didn't really add to us. It took away a lot of the fun, to have to be in this grown-up stuff," Mollin said. "We eventually just didn't think it was going to work."

Two Oscar wins later, Hilary Swank is still not over being fired from Beverly Hills, 90210 back in the day.

After playing single mom Carly Reynolds for 13 episodes in season eight, Swank was unexpectedly fired despite having signed a two-year contract, leaving her "devastated" after learning fans didn't love her character paired with Steve Sanders.

"They were like, 'Look, it's not working,'" Swank said on Conan of the conversation she had with producers. "And I couldn't move. I was like, 'What's not working? Me? Am I bad? I'm not working because I'm bad?'"

But when one door closes, another opens, and soon after her firing Swank landed her (first) Oscar-winning role in 1999's Boys Don't Cry.
