#756. Off Campus Season 2 Premiere Date Revealed

Off Campus season two is skating to screens this spring with Stephen Kalyn's Dean Di Laurentis and Mika Abdalla's Allie Hayes romance taking center ice. Keep reading for everything to know.

Off Campus is ready to bring the heat back to Briar University's ice.

After all, the hockey romance is returning with more games, love and betrayal in its highly anticipated second season on April 28, the series confirmed on social media.

Stephen Kalyn, who plays hockey star Dean Di Laurentis, answered a knock at the door, asking the camera in the Nov. 5 Instagram video, "What? Did you miss us?" Mika Abdalla, who is returning as theater student Allie Hayes, added, "Dean and Allie are officially back for season two," before the door closed with the show's premiere date on the sign.

The second installment kicks off after an explosive season one finale, which ended when a love triangle between Allie, Dean, and fellow hockey player Hunter Davenport (Charlie Evans) came to a head in the form of a blowout fight.

The charged encounter set the stage for friends-with-benefits Dean and Allie—the best friend of Hannah Wells (Ella Bright), last season's leading lady opposite Garrett Graham (Belmont Cameli)—to step into center ice, with their game-winning romance acting as the main storyline for season two.

Meanwhile, John Logan (Antoni Cipriano) will be skating through the early chapters of his own love story with Grace Ivers (India Fowler).

"We are so excited to continue Allie and Dean's story as our primary romance of season 2 after kickstarting their romance in season 1," showrunner Louisa Levy announced in a May statement. "But if you fell in love with Hannah and Garrett, don't worry—they will still be an integral part of our robust ensemble."

Though Dean and Allie's love story is part of Elle Kennedy's third novel The Score—Logan and Grace are the leads of the second, The Mistake—Levy noted the momentum of the first season led to the change-up.

"I wanted viewers to know who they were going to be tuning in for next," she told Variety at the time. "Allie felt so organic, because she's Hannah's best friend and Dean is already there, and their love story in the book is a secret—so why not let it be a surprise, even to book fans, when we're going to launch it?"

"Some things had to work a little differently because of the timing and the way we platform them," she continued, "but I promise all the fan-favorite things are still intended and planned. There's still a lot of road with those two."

For instance, Hunter—whom Allie had a one-night stand with before seeing the animosity between him and Dean, which prompted the aforementioned brawl—was necessary as an antagonist in the Prime Video show.

"He also comes from the same world as Dean, which made his arrival feel organic," she explained. "We needed to throw a wrench into Dean and Allie's arrangement to elongate their story, and pulling from that universe felt right."

For Kennedy's part, the author is looking forward to seeing Logan and Grace's budding romance begin to play out.

"I did get to see the chemistry tests with Antonio and India, who is cast as Grace, and they are spectacular together," she told E! News ahead of the season one premiere. "That's what I'm probably most excited for."

"She rambles when she's nervous and she's just so random," she added of the new character. "I think people will really resonate with her because she is just awkward. There are moments where, in the book, I was writing it and I was cringing, I'm like, 'No, Grace, shut up!' I'm very excited to see that."

While fans wait to lace up their skates for Off Campus season two, keep reading for more must-watch romance TV shows.

Fan of hot hockey players, passionate sex, a slow burn and a rivals-to-lovers trope?

Look no further than the Crave original series—based on Rachel Reid's Gamechangers books—that follows Montreal Voyageurs captain Shane Hollander (Hudson Williams) and Boston Bears captain Ilya Rozanov (Connor Storrie) through their decade-long romance.

The on-ice rivals spent years in a push-and-pull of clandestine hookups in hotel rooms while soaring to new heights in their hockey careers. But as deeper feelings begin melting any ice in their hearts, they are forced to come to terms with what they really want—and its potential fallout.

But don't worry, show creator Jacob Tierney proved he'll always be Shane and Ilya's biggest cheerleader.

"This is a gay love story set in the world of hockey, so its very existence is an act of rebellion," he told Toronto Life in November 2025. "But the show itself is happily ever after. I didn't want to subvert too many romance tropes—I love these stories. This show is queer joy for adults."

For Belly Conklin (Lola Tung), everything good, everything magical happens between the months of June and August in the Amazon Video series, based on Jenny Han's book series of the same name.

But summer proves to be different when the 15-year-old returns to the beachfront town with brother Steven Conklin (Sean Kaufman) and mom Laurel Park (Jackie Chung) to visit their mom's best friend Susannah Fisher (Rachel Blanchard).

This time, the teen finds herself in a love triangle with brothers Conrad Fisher (Christopher Briney) and Jeramiah Fisher (Gavin Casalegno) amid the throes of adolescence in this emotional coming-of-age series.

When it comes to this sports drama, watching it with clear eyes and full hearts means you'll never lose.

The five-season series, which ran from 2006 to 2011, follows Coach Eric Taylor (Kyle Chandler) as he guides the Dillon Panthers to victory in a football-obsessed town while navigating personal and professional pressures.

At the center of this beloved series—also starring Jesse Plemons, Michael B. Jordan, Minka Kelly, Jurnee Smollett, to name just a few—is the bond between Coach and his wife Tami (Connie Britton), who work as an anchor for the team.

"We really wanted to deal with the authenticity of what it is to try to make a marriage work," Britton told NPR in 2011. "If you're in what we'd consider to be a good marriage, there's going to be a foundation there. There's going to be a foundation that is solid."

"So on top of that foundation," she continued, "you can rock the boat every which way that you want to, and be able to go back to what's at the core of it."

The early-aughts were full of teen dramas where angst, romance and love were at the center. And One Tree Hill didn't wanna be anything other than that.

Set in the fictional town of Tree Hill, N.C., half-brothers Lucas Scott (Chad Michael Murray) and Nathan Scott (James Lafferty) learn to co-exist after the former is recruited to their school's basketball team.

With Lucas considered a social outcast to everyone except best friend Haley James (Bethany Joy Lenz) while being raised solely by his mom Karen Roe (Moira Kelly), the teen is forced to grapple with a new normal.

In his case, that means playing basketball with his brother—who continues to deal with the pressure from their dad Dan Scott (Paul Johansson)—becoming popular after joining the team and navigating a complicated love triangle between best friends Peyton Sawyer (Hilary Burton) and Brooke Davis (Sophia Bush).

Ryan Atwood (Ben McKenzie), an incredibly intelligent teen with problems at home, finds himself living with an affluent family in the cushy town of Newport Beach thanks to his public defender Sandy Cohen (Peter Gallagher).

As he gets closer to his future best friend Seth Cohen (Adam Brody) in the four-season series, Ryan is swept away by the glitz, glamour and drama of Newport Beach, which includes the misunderstood it-girl Marissa Cooper (Mischa Barton) and her fiery best friend Summer Roberts (Rachel Bilson).

A teen love triangle meets the rural town of Silver Falls, Colorado.

Jackie Howard (Nikki Rodriguez) finds herself living with her mom's best friend Katherine Walter (Sarah Rafferty) on a farm after her family died in a car accident.

Now, thousands of miles from her hometown of New York City, Jackie tries to acclimate to a town that has more cattle than people while grieving the loss of her family, all while developing feelings for Katherine's sons Cole Walter (Noah LaLonde) and Alex Walter (Ashby Gentry).

After the popularity of the To All The Boys I Loved Before trilogy, based on Jenny Han's three-book series, fans returned to the Covey household as the youngest sister Kitty (Anna Cartcart) embarks on a journey of self-discovery at South Korea's KISS Academy.

While juggling a new school, Kitty explores her own sexuality and friendships, as well as learns more about her late mom, who also attended the academy as a teen.

The Australian three-season show—a reboot of the 1994 series of the same name—follows Amerie Wadia (Ayesha Madon) as she navigates Hartley High with her new friends Darren Rivers (James Majoos) and Quinni Gallagher-Jones (Chloé Hayden) after an explosive friendship fallout with BFF Harper McLean (Asher Yasbincek).

Once Amerie and Harper's map of all the students' sex lives is discovered, everyone is forced to attend a new sexual education class called Sexual Literacy Tutorial (SLT, though students pronounced it "sluts.")

From threesomes and wild sex to navigating the grief surrounding abortions and sexual assault, Heartbreak High pushes the envelope when it comes to its storyline.

If you are not from down under, a guide to Australian slang will be your best friend while watching this dramedy.

If you're looking for a college-centered series set in the world of fraternities and sororities, consider rushing this ABC Family show. The four-season series follows nerd Rusty Cartwright (Jacob Zachar) at Cyprus-Rhodes University as he explores Greek life at Kappa Tau Gamma, led by his appointed big brother Cappie (Scott Michael Foster).

Meanwhile, his sister Casey Cartwright (Spencer Grammer) is a member of Beta Zeta and Cappie's ex-girlfriend. The series follows six chapters at CRU, where parties, drama and excitement ensue. Oh, and a lot of beer pong.

In this German-language series on Amazon Video, Ruby Bell (Harriet Herbig-Matten) turns the extremely affluent Beaufort family's lives upside down after she sees Lydia (Sonja Weiber) having an affair with their teacher Graham Sutton (Eidin Jalali). Lydia's twin brother James (Damian Hardung), in an attempt to ensure Ruby's silence, tries to bribe her with money and then with his body.

An unimpressed Ruby—a low-income student on scholarship at the tony prep school—declined both of the arrogant lacrosse stars' deals. But while the pair initially despises one another, it doesn't take long before that frustration turns into passion.

All that's left is for Ruby and James to navigate their budding feelings while grappling with the repercussions of their socioeconomic differences. Will love be enough for a happily ever after?

You really shouldn't wanna wait to take the metaphorical trip to Capeside for this six-season series centering Dawson Leery (James Van Der Beek) and his best friends Joey Potter (Katie Holmes) and Pacey Witter (Joshua Jackson).

The show begins with 15-year-old aspiring filmmaker Dawson and his BFF Joey, who is not-so-secretly in love with him, as they navigate adolescence with their friends in the fictional Massachusetts town. Along with exploring topics such as first love, teen pregnancy, racism, drugs and more, the series was a trailblazer in queer media.

The season three finale, which aired in May 2004, featured the first romantic kiss between two gay men Jack Mcphee (Kerr Smith) and Ethan Brody (Adam Kaufman).

"[The scene] gave millions of people a storyline that was reflective of their reality," Kaufman told Us Weekly in May 2020. "I'm so honored to have been a part of that."

#754. Travis Kelce Teases Holiday Plans After Taylor Swift Wedding

Travis Kelce couldn’t hold back his excitement as he prepares for his first holiday season with his now-wife Taylor Swift.

Travis Kelce is ready to leave the Christmas lights up until at least January.

This is his and Taylor Swift’s place, and they’re making the rules as they head into the holiday season hot off the heels of their July nuptials.

“I’m excited for my first holiday as a married man,” Kelce told WWD Nov. 5 while in conversation about his new campaign with Tommy Hilfiger. “I love all the old traditions and can’t wait to start some new ones.”

And as soon as the Christmas lights start to glisten, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end will be simply having a wonderful Christmastime.

As he put it, “I start celebrating as that tree goes up.”

But that begs the question, did he ever stop celebrating since he said, “I do,” in New York City?

After all, the 37-year-old previously called his and Swift’s wedding “the best night of my life.”

“Marrying Taylor was more than I could have ever dreamed it to be,” he added during his September convo with ESPN’s Chris Berman, “because of all the people that showed up, and the amount of, you know, love that was in the air."

In fact, Kelce and Swift had to make their way through a crowd of nearly 1,000 well-wishers who descended on New York’s Madison Square Garden to witness the next chapter in the pair’s love story.

“Me and Taylor are so thankful for everybody that showed up,” Kelce said during the Sept. 2 episode of his New Heights podcast with brother Jason Kelce. “From the vows to the seeing everyone to how much fun we had throughout the entire evening, and hearing that being relayed through everyone’s stories of that night—it was just so magical man, I wish it could have lasted longer than it did."

For the Kansas City Chiefs player, one of the most particularly enchanting aspects of the evening was seeing all their loved ones from the furthest corners of their lives come together.

“It was so cool to see everyone from my childhood not only mesh with Taylor, but [the people] from her childhood and her family and friends," he explained, "and people that she works with to people that we’ve encountered over the course of our career and who we just admire as people and have become good friends with now."

For a look back at how Swift and Kelce went from strangers to the perfect teammates, read on.

Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's love story began in July 2023, when the singer's Eras Tour made a stop at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Mo.

As a huge Swiftie, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end caught the show with hopes of giving Taylor a friendship bracelet with his number on it. However, he failed to complete the pass due to her pre-show rituals.

"I was disappointed that she doesn't talk before or after her shows because she has to save her voice for the 44 songs that she sings," Travis shared on the July 26 episode of his New Heights podcast. "So, I was a little butt-hurt I didn't get to hand her one of the bracelets I made for her."

After publicly recounting his fumble—a move Taylor would later describe as "metal as hell"—Travis decided to shoot his shot and invite the Grammy winner to watch the Chiefs play at Arrowhead Stadium.

"I threw it out there, I threw the ball in her court," he shared on The Pat McAfee Show. "I told her, you know, 'I've seen you rock the stage in Arrowhead, you might have to come see me rock the stage in Arrowhead and see which one's a little more lit.' So, we'll see what happens in the near future."

Travis was rocking a mustache—which he debuted in August during training camp—when he was first introduced to Taylor.

As he later noted of the era, "That 'stache and the 87 jersey was pretty iconic there for a little bit, and I had it when I met Taylor for the first time."

By early September, a source close to the situation told E! News that Travis and Taylor were "texting and talking here and there."

"It's been very low-key," the insider explained, "as he's been in season."

Accepting Travis' invite, Taylor joined the athlete's mom Donna Kelce at Arrowhead Stadium to watch him and the Chiefs take on the Chicago Bears. After the game, Taylor and Travis were seen packing PDA at a local bar.

Though folklore had it that it was the couple's first in-person meeting, the "Karma" singer later clarified the two had spent a "significant amount of time" getting to know each other beforehand.

As Taylor noted, "We would never be psychotic enough to hard launch a first date."

As an indication that the relationship was heating up, Taylor brought her squad—including friends Blake Lively, Ryan Reynolds, Sophie Turner, Hugh Jackman, Sabrina Carpenter and Antoni Porowski—to watch the Chiefs play against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

Another sign that Travis could be The 1? Taylor started bonding with Brittany Mahomes—the wife of Travis' BFF and teammate Patrick Mahomes—in and outside of NFL games.

The couple took their romance to TV, making a surprise appearance on the Oct. 14 episode of Saturday Night Live. Their Big Apple takeover also included the after-party for the NBC sketch show and a date night at the Waverly Inn.

During a bye week, Travis traveled down to Argentina to catch the South American leg of Taylor's Eras Tour. Not only did the NFL star bond with Taylor's dad, Scott Swift, at the Nov. 11 show in Buenos Aires, but he also got a special shoutout from the stage.

"Karma is that guy on the Chiefs," Taylor sang, "coming straight home to me."

After the show, the Midnights artist was seen running up to Travis backstage and greeting him with a passionate kiss.

Taylor addressed the lavender craze surrounding her appearances at Travis' games.

"I'm going to see him do what he loves, we're showing up for each other, other people are there and we don't care," she told Time. "The opposite of that is you have to go to an extreme amount of effort to make sure no one knows that you're seeing someone."

The music superstar turned Travis' Dec. 17 game into a family affair, bringing her dad to cheer on her man.

Taylor and Travis spent their first New Year's Eve together, sharing a romantic kiss when the clock struck midnight on Jan. 1.

Continuing to bond with Travis' family, Taylor hung out with his brother Jason Kelce and sister-in-law Kylie Kelce at the Chiefs' game against the Buffalo Bills.

Taylor joined Travis on the football field when the Chiefs won the AFC Championship, a victory that cemented the team's spot in the 2024 Super Bowl. The couple shared a celebratory kiss before exchanging the L-word.

"Tay, I'm gonna enjoy with the guys," he told her. "I love you—so much it's not funny."

The pair locked lips on the field after Travis led the Kansas City Chiefs to victory on Feb. 11, 2024 in Las Vegas.

Taylor posted footage of Travis on social media for the first time Feb. 12, poking fun at how she took her parents clubbing with the athlete after the Super Bowl.

Taylor's first Instagram pic featuring Travis was a selfie of the two with Prince William and his and wife Kate Middleton's eldest kids Prince George and Princess Charlotte backstage at the singer's Eras tour show at Wembley Stadium in London.

While attending his seventh Eras tour concert, and second show at London's Wembley Stadium, the NFL star joined his girlfriend onstage as a backup performer during her performance of "I Can Do It With a Broken Heart."

Taylor joined Travis for the Chief's first game of the regular 2024-25 season and appeared to re-enact a PDA moment from October 2023 in this photo shared by Chariah Gordon, who is pictured with her boyfriend, Chiefs wide receiver Mecole Hardman.

The two attended model Karen Elson's wedding to Electric Lady Studios owner Lee Foster in New York City.

The next day, the pair attended the men's singles final match at the U.S. Open.

The two stepped out for a double dinner date with Blake Lively and Ryan Reynolds in NYC.

The pair stepped out for two back-to-back dates in New York City over the last weekend of 2024, matching outfits both times.

The pair spent the NFL off-season together, enjoying a snowy vacation to Montana with sportscaster Erin Andrews.

Travis posted his first pics with Taylor on Instagram in July 2025, including an adorable shot of them at dinner—which subtly revealed their phone lockscreen pics of one another.

August: 2025: Taking Their Romance to New Heights

Self-described New Heights superfan Taylor made her debut on Travis and Jason's podcast in a nearly two-hour-long special episode Aug. 13. In addition to very candidly detailing their life together—in and out of the spotlight—Taylor also revealed her 12th studio album The Life of a Showgirl, set to debut Oct. 3.

August 2025: She'd Marry Him With Paper Rings

More than two years after Travis' podcast shoutout heard 'round the world, Travis and Taylor announced they are engaged. Making a cheeky reference to her song "So High School." the two captioned the Aug. 26 Instagram post featuring their engagement photos, "Your English teacher and your gym teacher are getting married."

While Taylor would've married Travis with paper rings, the athlete popped the question with an old mine brilliant cut diamond sparkler he co-designed with Artifex Fine Jewelry's Kindred Lubeck.

October 2025: The Life of a Showgirl in Love

Taylor released The Life of a Showgirl, her 12th studio album that she recorded during the Eras Tour. Songs about her romance with Travis include "The Fate of Ophelia"—which included many Easter eggs about the NFL star—and "Wood," in which she cheekily sang that his "love was the key that opened my thighs.”

"New Heights of manhood," Taylor continued on the track, referencing the name of Travis' podcast. "I ain't gotta knock on wood."

Taylor and Travis made their first award show appearance as a couple at the 2026 iHeartRadio Music Awards, where she won seven trophies including Pop Album of the Year for The Life of a Showgirl.

"The Life of a Showgirl was really inspired by the energy that I felt like looking into crowds and seeing you guys every single night," she told fans in the audience. "This album probably also feels very happy and confident and free because that's the way that I get to feel every single day of my life because of my fiancé, who's here tonight."

Taylor added as a nod to her "The Fate of Ophelia" lyrics, "So, thanks for all the vibes."

Ahead of their highly anticipated wedding, the couple enjoyed a PDA-filled date night at a New York Knicks vs. Cleveland Cavaliers game in Travis' hometown.

#752. 'Clock is ticking' - Gateshead fans fear for future

Gateshead are bottom of the National League with four points from 15 games

Fans of troubled National League Gateshead fear for its very existence as they wait to see if fresh investment comes forward to save the club.

The Tynside club desperately need new owners to step in after director Mark Nellist resigned and withdrew his funding support in September.

It appeared American private investment company, Flacks Group, would buy the club but their takeover was delayed and players and staff have not been paid this month.

Against this backdrop, the football team is bottom of the league with four points from 15 games, without a permanent manager and they have lost their past nine league matches.

"It's very worrying," David Geddess of the Heed Army podcast told BBC Look North (North East and Cumbria). "I seriously think it could be the end of the club.

"Financial issues are all over football but at the minute Gateshead play in a rented stadium and we have no assets. If anyone wants to take anything out of the club, it means winding up the club."

Prospective Gateshead takeover close to collapse

Gateshead to be sold to American investment group

Troubled Gateshead fail to pay September wages

Gateshead are the smallest club in the National League, operating on average attendances this season of just 643 at their rented home, the Gateshead International Stadium.

Off-the-field issues are nothing new but they have come to a head in the past few months.

Under Rob Elliot, they recovered from a dreadful winter of 16 successive losses in all competitions to collect 31 points from 15 matches to produce an incredible survival act.

With that achieved, American-based businessman Stephen Paylor agreed a deal to become the club's co-owner alongside Nellist.

Elliot left for Carlisle United in the close season with ex-Middlesbrough and Sunderland midfielder Lee Cattermole appointed in his first job as a number one.

Results on the pitch were already spiralling downwards when Nellist withdrew his financial support for the club at the end of September.

Without that, wages for players and staff were delayed as they waited for fresh investment which looked to have arrived in the shape of Flacks Group.

They provided initial funds to pay wages, but last week the American group said in an open letter that the proposed takeover was on the brink of collapse.

They said another group, Shoreline Limited, had tried to buy the club in March and then filed court documentation four months later to confirm that its agreement was null and void, and therefore proceeded to enter negotiations with the current ownership.

With Shoreline not responding to requests to state that they were not interested in purchasing Gateshead, Flacks Group said that they could not carry on with their intended acquisition.

"We find ourselves bottom of the league and the club isn't the most attractive asset in the world to anybody," added Geddess.

"We then find ourselves with billionaire investors round the corner and you can't get it because of a legal issue with someone else that tried to buy the football club.

"It's such a mess. Then add HMRC in, it's really going to hit the fan."

Lee Cattermole was in charge for 12 National League games with Gateshead

Cattermole was dismissed on 4 October with Ben Clark in interim charge since then.

He finally claimed a win in his seventh game in charge on Tuesday as they beat Stoke City Under-21s in the National League Cup.

But they have lost all three league games and were thrashed 5-0 in an FA Cup replay by eighth-tier Stafford Rangers to dash any hopes of a decent cup run and even more important, a lucrative pay-day.

As such, they have not had a home league game since 3 October to boost deprived coffers while they are believed to owe more than Â£200,000 to HMRC.

A rearranged league fixture with Tamworth for this Saturday had to be postponed too, after discovering that two other large events were to be staged at the International Stadium on the same day, causing a clash.

The club's very existence is under threat and Mark Ferguson, MP for Gateshead Central and Whickham, spoke to the Independent Football Regulator on Wednesday.

"Right now, the future of the club is up in the air and we shouldn't be blind to that," said Mr Ferguson MP.

"The clock is ticking and whatever action people can take, if they want to get a resolution, that work needed to start yesterday."

Their predicament in the National League is bad enough, 13 points from safety, but for fans it goes far beyond those current struggles.

"On the pitch doesn't really matter at the minute," said Geddess.

"We want infrastructure, we want to be in a place where this doesn't happen again the future or the near future because it's happened too many times."

#751. TikToker Says Neighbor, 97, Died After Dancing at His Birthday Party

TikToker Eden Malinoff, who goes by BakedSoCal on the app, shared that her 97-year-old neighbor Vito died during his Halloween-themed birthday party.

One man's legacy is stayin' alive after an unfortunate end to his party.

A California man died at his 97th birthday bash after dancing to "Stayin' Alive" by the Bee Gees, baker Eden Malinoff shared on TikTok.

"You'd probably be surprised to find out that my friend group consists of 20-something and 30-something-year-olds, and then a 96-year-old man named Vito," she began in her Nov. 2 TikTok video. "This past week was Vito's 97th birthday, and in true Vito fashion, he wanted to celebrate by throwing a Halloween birthday rager."

"When I asked him earlier in the week what the key was to living such a long life, he told me it was, and I quote, 'to never drink cheap liquor,'" Malinoff, who baked his birthday cake, continued. "So, I was inspired to make him a red wine chocolate cake that sat on top like fine wine. Because if I learned one thing from Vito, it is to never let your age stop you."

The 24-year-old noted, however, that the soirée did not end as anticipated after Vito "made a dramatic exit."

"But if there's any way Vito could have chosen to go out, it would have been like this," she said. "He was surrounded by people he loved. We were celebrating his long and full life, and I am just so grateful that I got to be a part of it."

After the Baked SoCal founder left fans stunned by Vito's unexpected death, she shared more details about what really went down during the party.

"I fear Vito did unfortunately pass away at his 97th birthday party," she confirmed in a follow-up video on Nov. 4. "It was not planned. It was not intentional. We did not kill him. He was not intoxicated. It was just a freak coincidence."

Malinoff denied that the video was made "for clout," saying it was instead a celebration of Vito's colorful life.

"His death was such a reflection of that," she added. "He was such an icon, and I just wanted to share what an inspiration he was to me and the whole Venice community. Vito would have absolutely loved the attention that this video got, but that was not my intention at all."

#749. Kim Kardashian, Jennifer Lawrence Step Out for NYC Outing

Kim Kardashian and Jennifer Lawrence stepped outside the Four Seasons hotel in New York sporting matching SKIMS pajamas, proving their friendship is stronger than you think.

Odds are Kim Kardashian and Jennifer Lawrence are closer than you’d think.

After all, the All’s Fair actress and Oscar winner stepped out together arm-in-arm for a walk in New York Nov. 4, going so far to sport matching SKIMS Onyx Floral Deer Print Cami and Pan sleep sets.

Kim and Jennifer are all smiles while linking arms in photos and sporting matching shades and brown robes along with their pajamas, which are being sold as part of SKIMS new holiday campaign.

An avid reality TV fan, Jennifer’s friendship display with Kim has been a long time coming, as the Hunger Games actress has been a friend of the family for years—and a fan of their series.

“The Kardashians were just in Thailand,” Jennifer joked in an interview with Vanity Fair in 2014. “So that was a big deal.”

Also noting she was binging Real Housewives at the time, she quipped, “I’m trying to stay up-to-date on all the pointless gossip that goes on in Hollywood.”

Through the years, Jennifer has been a devout watcher of the family’s series, even joking to E! News that watching it can make her emotional.

“I was crying about the Kardashians the other night,” The Silver Linings Playbook actress revealed to E! in 2016. “They’re under a lot of pressure. Even if it’s elective, it’s pressure—and I get that!”

Kim, for her part, has revealed it was jarring for Jennifer to be a such a big fan of her—as the feeling was mutual.

“I was in NYC and I ran into Jennifer Lawrence,” she said during an E! International junket in 2015. “We said, 'Hi' and walked into the elevator and as the doors were closing, she screamed across the lobby, 'I love your show!' We were laughing so hard.”

Fast forward 10 years later, and the duo are stepping out of NYC hotels together. But trust, Jennifer is as devout to The Kardashians as ever, and even recently spilled her latest hot take on the series.

“Kourtney [Kardashian] is more annoying than ever,” she said in a Vanity Fair video segment released last year. “She drives me nuts.”

Lawrence wasn’t trying to be f--king rude, as Kim would say, but she had to get her irritation toward the eldest sister off her chest.

“Everything has to be an announcement,” she explained. “‘I’m not gonna wear outfits anymore.’ Just wear whatever you want. Don’t make an announcement about it. Or, ‘I don’t have a TV in my room.’ Just don’t watch TV. Stop announcing it.”

Unlike other reality TV fans, though, Lawrence got to see a direct response to her take airing on her favorite show.

In a recent episode of The Kardashians, Kourtney joked that if Jennifer wants to be considered the sixth sister in her family and share her opinions, “I'll f--king slap the s--t out of her.”

As the 47-year-old quipped, “Invite her over. And I’ll go for it like she’s my sister.”

For more Hollywood besties, keep reading…

Nicole, a longtime fan of her sister-in-law's movies, several years ago took the opportunity to ask her to re-enact a few of her favorite movie scenes, including one from My Best Friend's Wedding.

"We were in Chicago and I said to her, 'Cameron, I need you to give it to me. I need you to get behind the luggage cart and run towards me, towards the airport,'" she said on the Everything Iconic with Danny Pellegrino podcast in May 2024. "I really think like at a certain point, we were driving past things and I was like, 'Say this. Say this. Say this.' And she really just let me have it. It was very generous of her."

Thank goodness Lawrence is down to hang or we might have been robbed of one of our most beloved set of besties. Their friendship was born from an email the Oscar winner sent after watching Schumer's 2015 comedy. "I emailed her after I saw Trainwreck and said, 'I don't know where to get started. I guess I should just say it: I'm in love with you,'" she recalled to The New York Times. "We started emailing, and then emailing turned to texting." But what really solidified their bond was Schumer's casual invite for her new pal to join her and her high school friends in the Hamptons. Shocked when she said yes, Schumer relaxed when she realized Lawrence is "the coolest chick you'll ever meet," she said on The Daily Show. "She's the best hang, she was like one of the gang."

Who doesn't want a friend that basically owns real estate in your corner? They've been tight since falling in love at first sight at the 2004 premiere of Man on Fire. "It was one of those instant chemistry things where you just feel like, 'I love this person. I love being around this person. This person makes me laugh,'" Lopez recalled to Entertainment Tonight of her Brooklyn-bred bestie. And Remini was among those getting loud in celebration of Lopez's performance at President Joe Biden's inauguration. "I wrote her and said, 'You know, you're a girl from the Bronx. 'Like, what you did today was really inspiring, and it was just beautiful to watch," she told E! News. "Just beautiful.'"

The gold standard of celebrity besties—this trio has been in lock step since their days of sharing salads on the Warner Brothers lot. "They grew up together and went through this formidable life experience that was Friends," a source told E! News. So, much like you might meet up with coworkers from your first job, they make it a point to get happy hours (and the occasional major reunion) on their calendar. "Geographically it's not hard to be at Courteney's Sunday dinners or at a pool party at Jen's house," notes the source. "They all feel incredibly close and always will be."

Making other friends jealous since a chance meeting at improv training in 1993, the frequent costars are so close, they liken their bond to that of family. "I think that Tina and I are chosen sisters," Poehler, whose sole sibling is younger brother Greg, told PopSugar while discussing their 2015 flick Sisters. "I think we are chosen family, so I think it's been fun to experience that thing I never got to experience in real life."

"It was like, you know, how people say love at first sight? We had that thing," Philipps told Entertainment Weekly of their initial interaction on the Dawson's Creek set. "We had that friend connection. It was just an immediate: 'Of course we're drinking wine and smoking cigarettes and getting in bar fights.' We just had an immediate love for each other that's continued over the years." Fortunately for us, we get to voyeuristically follow along as they work red carpets, wear coordinating outfits and occasionally dye Williams' hair the most perfect shade of millennial pink.

Having had "women that were really helpful to me when I was pregnant," mom of two Washington has always strived to pay it forward with her celeb pals. "I really do try to have those conversations openly and honestly as possible, especially with my soul sister, with Eva," she told Entertainment Tonight. Her advice was well-received when Longoria welcomed son Santiago in 2018, with the Grand Hotel actress calling the Scandal alum, "basically my doula."

More than 20 years after nabbing Oscar gold, the Good Will Hunting scribes are back at it again, working on The Last Duel. And though it's been a minute since they shared a screen, their bromance hasn't wavered. "I've known him for 35 years, and we grew up together," Damon told Entertainment Tonight in 2016. "We were both in love with the same thing—acting and filmmaking. I think we fed on each other's obsession during really formative, important years and that bonded us for life."

The connection between two of television's most powerful women dates back to 1976 when they were working at a Baltimore station—though anchors (Winfrey helmed the 6 p.m. hour) and production assistants (that was King), didn't generally socialize. "The newsroom hierarchy," CBS This Morning cohost King recalled in their O Interview. But with a heavy snow coming down, Winfrey invited the $12,000-a-year PA to sleep at her house. "The next day," said Winfrey, "we went to the mall." And a friendship was born over Casual Corner sweaters.

Sure, your friend dates likely don't involve watching your pal play for Wimbledon and U.S. Open titles or get-togethers at a palace. But the bond between the tennis champ and the Duchess of Sussex began much like any other—over girl talk. "We hit it off immediately," Meghan wrote on her now-shuttered lifestyle website The Tig of their meeting at a 2014 Super Bowl event. "Taking pictures, laughing through the flag football game we were both playing in, and chatting not about tennis or acting, but about all the good old fashioned girly stuff."

Game of Thrones may have wrapped, but the relationship between the Stark sisters lives on. In fact Williams, who served as Turner's maid of honor when she wed Joe Jonas in 2019, is convinced the best thing to come of the eight-season HBO hit wasn't any of its 12 Emmy awards. "It was like one big elaborate thing to find me a best friend. This whole show!" she joked to E! News at the final season premiere. "I'm kidding. It's been incredible. To have a friend like that on something as wild as this is just like a godsend, really."

Friends gifted Aniston with more than one goals-worthy bestie. Before she and Witherspoon developed their Apple TV+ series, The Morning Show, they portrayed sisters on the NBC hit. "I was 23 years old and had just had a baby," the Oscar winner recalled to Harper's Bazaar of her two-episode arc back in 2000. "I was nursing Ava [Phillippe] on set, and Jen just kept going, 'You have a baby?' I was like, 'I know, it's weird.' And I remember her being like, 'Where are you going?' And I was like, 'I'm pumping!'" Though Witherspoon felt admittedly nervous, she said Aniston couldn't have been more sweet: "We've been friends ever since."

Equal parts intriguing and covetable, this pairing was solidified at The Comedy Central Roast of Justin Bieber in 2015 before they teamed up for their VH1 cooking show, Martha & Snoop's Potluck Dinner Party. "She different, ya know, than what I'm accustomed," the marijuana-loving 17-time Grammy winner told LA Weekly of the Westchester-based domestic doyenne. "But then again she's so what I'm accustomed to. 'Cause she people. She just look different and she was born in a different era, but if you hang out with her and chill with her, she just like anybody else. That's why it works, because she never says nothing that's crazy in my ears. It's always like, 'Damn, I thought you would say that. OK.' That's why we get down, that's why we connected, Martha. 'Cause it feels like holy matrimony, and not holy macaroni."

Theirs is a newer alliance, but no less desirable. After years of existing in the same orbit, the "Hotline Bling" rapper and the "Hello" songstress, who have over a dozen Grammys between them, began throwing out the idea of a collaboration. "I really want us to do an official remix," she told Canada's etalk of their well-coordinated hits. "I love Drake. I love Drake so much. I even got the coat that's in the video, I got it delivered the other day, I ordered it. The red one." He responded by saying, "I'd do anything with Adele. I'd literally go to Adele's house right now and do laundry for her." Instead, they grabbed a bite to eat and hit up an L.A. bowling alley. Next time, you know, call us on our cell phone.

#748. LIV Golf is Shutting Down: What to Know About Its End

LIV Golf announced it is shutting down after months of speculation about the future of the Saudi Arabia-backed PGA Tour competitor. Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau were among the league's top players.

The professional men’s golf tour, founded in 2021 as a competitor to the PGA Tour, announced it is officially closing up shop after months of speculation over its draining finances.

According to a Nov. 5 announcement on the league’s website, in April CEO Scott O’Neil and other LIV Golf leadership began working with independent advisors to “identify the best, value-maximizing path forward for the Company and its stakeholders.”

However, “in light of the current circumstances,” the announcement noted, "we believe shifting toward an orderly wind-down is the most responsible path forward for the League at this time. The dedication of LIV Golf’s players, employees, partners, and fans made everything the League accomplished possible.”

In his own statement, O’Neil reflected on building the league up from the rough.

"LIV Golf was fun, demanding, inspiring, at times challenging—but always rewarding,” he said. "We created memories that I hope will inspire a new generation of fans to follow, play, and fall in love with this great game.”

And though the league is headed towards a wind down, the announcement did note the company will remain open to and consider any “value-maximum alternatives” that might arise.

After its launch, LIV instantly caught the attention of the golf world by poaching players like Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau, Brooks Koepka and Phil Mickelson from the PGA Tour.

And while the future of the tour—which is named after the Roman numerals for 54 as a nod to its 54-hole tournaments—had remained up in the air for quite some time, O’Neil had assured staff in April that the company was on, or rather in, the green.

“I want to be crystal clear: Our season continues exactly as planned, uninterrupted and at full throttle," O’Neil wrote in the email, obtained by multiple outlets. "While the media landscape is often filled with speculation, our reality is defined by the work we do on the grass.”

Indeed, the CEO—who took over as head of the company in 2025 from Greg Norman—emphasized his confidence that the company would remain in a good spot through the end of 2026.

“We are heading into the heart of our 2026 schedule,” he continued, “with the full energy of an organization that is bigger, louder, and more influential than ever before.”

Considering the company was only five years old, O’Neil encouraged his employees to think of the growing unease toward the company as regular “startup pressure.”

“We signed up for this because we believe in disrupting the status quo,” he continued. “We have faced headwinds since the jump, and we've answered every time with resilience and grace. Now, we answer by doing what we do best: putting on the most compelling show in sports.”

Nevertheless, LIV’s recent scorecard read differently.

Last year, Eugenio Chacarra, who started his professional golf career with LIV in 2022 before exiting in 2025, criticized the tour for the way it treated him as a player.

“I see what it’s like to win on the PGA Tour and how your life changes, how you get major access and ranking points,” Chacarra said in an interview with Flushing It Golf. “On LIV, nothing changes; there is only money.”

The fate of the golfers currently under the LIV tour remains unclear, but Koepka previously made the jump from LIV to the PGA Tour earlier this year.

Meanwhile, PGA Tour golfer Max Homa told Golfweek in April it would be “ridiculous” to not allow LIV players into his own tour. As he put it, “Everyone deserves a place to play golf.”

#747. 'A void that is impossible to fill' - tributes paid at De Miguel funeral

Jesus de Miguel's funeral took place in the town of Navahermosa in Spain on Thursday

Jesus de Miguel's family said "the mark he has left on so many people" was something they would always remember as the footballer's funeral took place on Thursday.

The Tenerife forward, who was 30, died after suffering a serious injury during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

After colliding with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono, De Miguel lay motionless on the pitch while being treated by medical staff and was taken to hospital, where he died at 07:00 GMT on Tuesday.

Owono was sent off for the challenge and the game was abandoned.

De Miguel's funeral was held in his parents' hometown of Navahermosa, Toledo, about 125km from the Spanish capital Madrid.

His Tenerife team-mates carried his coffin before the service at San Miguel Arcangel.

Current Spain coach Luis de la Fuente was among the mourners, along with Real Madrid president Florentino Perez, Atletico Madrid chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin and former Real and Spain coach Jose Antonio Camacho.

De Miguel's agent, Manuel Hernandez, issued a statement on behalf of the family, which read: "Thank you for loving him, for remembering him and for being with us.

"We cannot find enough words to thank you for every message, every phone call and every gesture of affection we are receiving.

"Feeling such affection for Jesus and seeing the mark he has left on so many people is something we will always carry with us.

"Jesus leaves a void that is impossible to fill, but also cherished memories for all of us who were fortunate enough to share our lives with him."

Fans pay respects to Tenerife's De Miguel

Tributes have been paid to De Miguel, who joined Tenerife in the summer of 2025, with a minute's silence being held at all games in European competitions this week.

In a statement issued by his club Andorra on Wednesday, goalkeeper Owono said he was experiencing "the most difficult days of my life".

"I feel enormous pain over the loss of Jesus," he added. "I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him."

In the hours after the death was announced, mourners laid flowers and lit candles beneath a black and white image of De Miguel at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez - the stadium on the island of Tenerife, where Monday's game took place.

"We need to grieve in the peace and quiet that this situation demands," the statement added.

"We appreciate the affection, concern and expressions of support that his loss is inspiring, and we are deeply grateful to you all."

Spain coach and Real Madrid president attend De Miguel funeral

The Spanish footballers' union, the AFE, made a request on Thursday for all this weekend's matches to be postponed out of respect for De Miguel.

Tenerife's match at Granada and Andorra's game against Mallorca have already been postponed, as were several midweek cup fixtures.

However, all Spanish sides in European competition have played their games this week.

The AFE said of the weekend games: "The footballers have expressed their deep sorrow for this loss and do not believe that there are the psychological and humane conditions necessary for the competition to be played in normal circumstances."

The union said its members "in every category" believed "unanimously" that the matches should not be played.

#746. Kristen Bell Gives Sneak Peek at What's Thawing for Frozen 3

Kristen Bell shared an update on Frozen 3 after reprising her role as Princess Anna in the upcoming Walt Disney Animation Studios sequel.

Kristen Bell is sharing a glimpse into the unknown.

As production for Frozen 3 heats up, the Nobody Wants This actress detailed stepping back into Princess Anna’s shoes for the third installment in the beloved Disney animated film franchise.

“Honestly, I’m living my dreams. I'm really living my dreams right now,” Bell shared during an appearance on the Nov. 4 episode of The Jennifer Hudson Show. “At 46 years old, you can still live all of your dreams.”

And she also opened the door into singing what will surely be magical musical numbers.

“I recorded two songs on Friday of this past week,” Bell revealed to Jennifer Hudson. “I love them so much.”

Though fans will have to try to let go of any impatience since the third film won’t be hitting theaters until Nov. 24, 2027, the Veronica Mars alum looks forward to the finished product.

“I just am very proud of what's being written,” Bell shared, “and I'm very excited to share it with the world.”

And while it may seem like this is the first time in forever since there has been an update on Frozen 3, Bell and her costar Idina Menzel—who voices Elsa—recently shared how they made sure magic would flow once again for a third film immediately after Frozen 2 was released in 2019.

“The second [Frozen 2] was over I was waiting by the phone and/or texting everyone, ‘When are we gonna do it?’” Bell told E! News in August. “And so I was in an anticipatory place.”

But Menzel emphasized that the Mouse House is always intentional with its moves and will “wait for the right time.”

“They're super patient with it,” she shared. “I guess we were a little impatient because we really like to get back to the process. We love being together. We love revisiting these characters.”

As for what more fans can expect when it’s time to build a snowman once more? Disney Animation head Jared Bush proved that some things may never truly change as Frozen 3 will tell “a very special story” like its predecessors.

That said, he teased to Collider in an interview published Nov. 3 the tale is “one that will surprise people.”

Until Frozen 3 soars into theaters next year, don’t hold your excitement back anymore and read for Frozen secrets…

1. An adaptation of Hans Christian Andersen's 1845 fairy tale The Snow Queen, Frozen was actually in development at Disney for almost a decade (and was briefly considered for a hand-drawn animated feature back in 1937).

The first modern attempt happened in 2002, and when 2003 also proved unsuccessful, more stalled attempts followed over the years. Frozen really didn't start coming together until Christopher Buck, who directed Tarzan, came aboard in 2008, but the film wasn't commissioned until 2011 following Tangled's box office success.

And in 2012, Jennifer Lee, who initially came on as a screenwriter, was named co-director, making her the first woman to direct an animated film by Walt Disney Animation Studios.

2. The movie was going to be titled The Snow Queen after the original fairy tale, but the filmmakers decided to change it to Frozen "because, to us, it represents the movie. Frozen plays on the level of ice and snow but also the frozen relationship, the frozen heart that has to be thawed," producer Peter Del Vecho explained to Bleeding Cool, denying it was inspired by Tangled. (The Snow Queen title was still used overseas.)

3. Idina Menzel and Kristen Bell auditioned and met with the producers of Tangled for the role of Rapunzel, which ultimately went to Mandy Moore. (Santino Fontana, who gave life to Anna's temporary fiancé Hans, originally auditioned for the role of Flynn in the 2010 film as well).

Bell, whose dream since she was a little girl was to voice a Disney character, was the "very first actress" to audition for Anna, with Lee saying, "We did audition a lot of people for that but she was the first and the best. We just fell in love with her."

4. Menzel's audition for Elsa, meanwhile, was actually a table-read with Bell before both had been officially cast, according to Lee.

"They read the whole script and at the end—we didn't have any songs written yet—and what they did was sing a duet and they sung 'Wind Beneath My Wings,' but they sung it like sisters and what you mean to me," she explained. "And there wasn't a dry eye in the house after they sang...that is when they knew, that was the whole potential and understanding the power of music and of what this emotional story can be."

5. In the early versions of the project, Elsa was actually the villain of the story (with one of the early concept art designs being inspired by Bette Midler and her "showgirl stage presence"), according to former Disney animation designer Claire Keane, who released the image on her web site.

"Originally, she was much more villainous," Buck allowed to Nerdist. "It's very easy to go in that direction for that type of character, but as the time went and we evolved the story, she became much more three-dimensional. Before, I thought she was one-dimensional but a very fully fleshed out character."

The moment the character really changed, though, was after they watched earlier cuts and realized it wasn't exactly working: "Someone came up with the brilliant idea...'what if the protagonist, Anna, and Elsa were related?'" art director Michael Giaimo revealed. "Because they weren't always siblings, they weren't always related, and that was the beginning of finding these characters."

6. The hardest character for the Frozen team to nail down aside from Elsa was actually Olaf, who was originally then-villainous Elsa's first guard.

"She created these snowman guards and Marshmallow was kind of a holdover from that because he was this scary snowman guard. Olaf was the very first guard she created," Buck explained, adding he was still funny at that time.

After changing the character of Elsa completely, it wasn't until the directors first sat down with Josh Gad that they found the character. "Josh adlibbed the line 'it's like a baby unicorn' and there was something about that innocence," Del Vecho told Kidz World.

7. One main character who wasn't originally in the movie was Hans, Anna's suitor-turned-villain, with Giaimo explaining, "Hans was never originally in the story in older versions...Kristoff always was in the story or a version of the Kristoff character and Anna. And then Hans was brought in at one point but he wasn't always a villain who turned initially, and then someone came up with the idea of him turning. He was always potentially a villain, but we gave it away much sooner."

8. Anna's oft-repeated "Wait what?" catchphrase? An ad-lib by Bell. She also slipped in one slightly off-color joke. "We slid it under the radar," she detailed to Vanity Fair of Anna's singing, "For years I've roamed these empty halls / Why have a ballroom with no balls?" The NSFW lyric almost got snipped, she admitted, "But then we were like, 'What are you talking about? That’s not what it means. Don’t be a perv.'"

11. After having a few of the first songs they originally composed for the film not make it in, songwriting couple Robert Lopez and Kristen Anderson-Lopez were feeling a little low, so they went for walk in Brooklyn's Prospect Park.

Listening to songs by Adele and Avril Lavigne and being surrounded by nature, Anderson-Lopez told Playbill, "We were in this kind of emo place of imagining what it would be like to be this perfect person who messed up once, and was chased away from everything she has known and all the people she has been sacrificing for."

Within a day, they would write the film's most iconic song that would go on to sell over 10 million copies in 2014 and win the Oscar for Best Original Song. All together now, "Let it go, let it goooooooo."

12. And after hearing "Let It Go" for the first time, Lee said she knew they had to rework the character of Elsa and her motivations completely.

"Half of us were crying. And then I just went, 'I have to rewrite the whole movie,'" she said on the Scriptnotes podcast. "I really, it was—I was just like I'm going to go lie down for a couple minutes. But it was the best thing. We knew we had the movie."

13. On the same podcast, Lee admitted there was "a lot of push and pull" when it came to Elsa's look after her transformation via "Let It Go" and how sexy to make her after this awakening.

"Everyone was seduced by her. And so there was this tug of war I think, a bit, of letting people have a little—people who wanted to have that a little and not be afraid of it, but not make it a sexual statement," the co-director explained. "It's more a moment of, for me, it was like you strut and you say nobody is looking, this is what I'm going to—I'm not going to be afraid of my sexuality. I'm not going to be afraid of who I am. I'm not going to be afraid of anything about myself."

14. After eagle-eyed fans spotted one of many easter eggs in the film—Tangled's Rapunzel (post haircut) and Eugene briefly appearing in a scene during the morning of Elsa's coronation—a compelling fan theory that tied together Frozen, Tangled and Little Mermaid surfaced: Anna and Elsa's parents died when their boat sank...what if it was when they were on their way to the Tangled pair's wedding? And what if the sunken ship in The Little Mermaid is the ship they were sailing on?!

15. This theory only works if you believe Anna and Elsa's parents actually did die in the shipwreck, something Buck speculated about in a Reddit AMA, saying, in his mind, the King and Queen of Arendelle, as well as their "baby boy," did not actually die after being shipwrecked. (Who knew they had a son?)

He said they washed up on the shore of a jungle and built "a tree house" before being "eaten by a leopard." That baby boy? Tarzan, of course.

"That's my fun little world," he later told MTV. While the theory isn't official (and definitely takes a hit when you factor in the events of Frozen II), Buck said, "Whatever people want to believe, go for it. If you want to tie them all together, then do it."

16. The original ending of the film was drastically different, with the earlier versions, of course, presenting Elsa as the villain and not having Anna and Elsa related.

Beginning with a prophecy about "a ruler with a frozen heart will bring destruction to the kingdom of Arendelle," viewers would learn Elsa became the Snow Queen after she was left at the altar and decided to freeze her own heart, according to EW.

By the end of the film, Anna convinces Elsa to use her powers to save Arendelle from an avalanche started by Hans, with the ultimate reveal being the prophecy was actually about the two-faced prince. (Elsa's heart would then unfreeze, making her capable of love again.)

"The problem was that we felt like we had seen it before," Del Vecho told EW of the original ending. "It wasn't satisfying. We had no emotional connection to Elsa—we didn't care about her because she had spent the whole movie being the villain. We weren't drawn in. The characters weren't relatable."

#745. Ronaldo's most iconic moments as he retires from international football

Cristiano Ronaldo became the first player to win five Champions League trophies and remains the top scorer in the tournament's history

Cristiano Ronaldo says his international career with Portugal is over, meaning the 41-year-old will just play on with Al-Nassr.

The main thing driving him on now is hoping to reach an unprecedented 1,000 career goals - he is currently on 985.

BBC Sport looks at some of the most iconic moments of a career that has also taken in spells at Sporting, Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus.

Ronaldo spurred on by 1,000 goals and Portugal glory

Ronaldo will not retire until he scores 1,000 goals

Untouchable or a support act? Ronaldo's 1,000-goal quest continues

Cristiano Ronaldo had one season in the Sporting first team before moving to Old Trafford

After 31 first-team games and five goals for Sporting, Ronaldo caught the eye of Manchester United in a pre-season friendly in 2003, setting up two goals in a 3-1 win in Lisbon.

Ronaldo revealed that United boss Alex Ferguson took him into the dressing room afterwards to meet the players.

Five days later he joined the Red Devils for Â£12m.

"After we played Sporting the lads in the dressing room talked about him constantly, and on the plane back from the game they urged me to sign him - that's how highly they rated him," said Ferguson.

"He is one of the most exciting young players I've ever seen."

Cristiano Ronaldo has won league titles in England, Spain, Italy and Saudi Arabia

Ronaldo won the FA Cup in his first season at United, scoring in the final against Millwall.

But it was in 2006-07 that his career really exploded. He hit 17 Premier League goals, his first season of double figures, was named player of the year and young player of the year - and won his first league title.

The following season was even better, winning his first Champions League - scoring in the final - his first European Golden Shoe for top scorer, and another league title.

Cristiano Ronaldo won the first Puskas award - and it remains the only Champions League goal to win it

Ronaldo scored 118 goals in 292 games in his first spell at United, and one was ranked above all the others.

He hit an absolute rocket of a shot into the top corner from 40 yards in his homeland against Porto, a goal which took them into the Champions League semi-finals.

It won the inaugural Fifa Puskas award for goal of the year.

Months later, Ronaldo joined Real Madrid for Â£80m.

Cristiano Ronaldo helped Real Madrid to win their first Copa del Rey in seven years

Ronaldo's first season at Real Madrid produced no trophies and his second saw just the Copa del Rey won.

That final was especially notable because it is the first time Ronaldo had scored the winning goal in a final. And it was in El Clasico, one of four meetings in 18 days in all competitions.

He rose at the far post to power in a trademark header from Angel di Maria's cross in extra time as Real beat Barcelona 1-0.

Cristiano Ronaldo scored 14 goals in 14 games against Levante

Ronaldo, then 30, scored in a 3-0 La Liga win over Levante in October 2015 to become the club's all-time top scorer with his 324th goal in 310 games.

The 2015-16 campaign would go on to be the sixth season in a row that Ronaldo scored 50 or more goals in all competitions.

Ronaldo ended up extending that record by 126 goals - leaving Real with 450 goals in just 438 games.

Cristiano Ronaldo is the top scorer in European Championship history - with 14 goals - as well as lifting the trophy once

The one thing missing from Ronaldo's CV was international success.

And that came in 2016 when Portugal won the European Championship by beating hosts France 1-0 in the final in Paris.

Ronaldo ended up taking on an unofficial coaching role in that final after going off injured in tears midway through the first half.

He was named in the team of the tournament after three goals and three assists. Ronaldo retires as the top scorer in Euros history, with 14 goals.

Cristiano Ronaldo has won five Ballons d'Or, only behind Lionel Messi

Cristiano Ronaldo won his fifth Ballon d'Or, equalling Lionel Messi's record at the time, after winning the Champions League and La Liga in 2016-17. He netted twice in that European final over Juventus.

It followed on from the best player in the world awards in 2008, 2013, 2014 and 2016.

Sadly for Ronaldo, Messi would go on to win three more Ballons d'Or, meaning he won their personal rivalry 8-5.

Cristiano Ronaldo scored one of his eight Champions League hat-tricks in the 2017 win over Bayern Munich

Ronaldo became the first player to score 100 Champions League goals with a hat-trick in the 2016-17 quarter-final second leg win over Bayern Munich.

Only Messi and Robert Lewandowski have joined him to date in the century club.

Ronaldo would go on to score 141 goals in 187 games (also a record) in Europe's top competition. For six seasons in a row he was the tournament's top scorer or joint top scorer.

"That is one of the great goals you will seeâ¦ I was going to say Champions League football, but, basically, football," said Pat Nevin in BBC Radio 5 Live commentary

In 2018 came one of the most iconic moments of Ronaldo's career, maybe the greatest Champions League goal ever scored.

In the quarter-final, Ronaldo leapt into the air before acrobatically firing into the corner of the net with an incredible bicycle kick against Juventus.

Even the Juve fans stood up to applaud the player who would join their club months later.

It was nominated for the Puskas Award but he finished second to Mohamed Salah's goal for Liverpool against Everton.

The night Juventus rose to applaud Ronaldo

Cristiano Ronaldo was the first man to win five Champions Leagues, although he was not the last as Real Madrid kept winning it without him

Ronaldo won two La Liga titles and two Copa del Rey trophies at Real Madrid, but it was in Europe's elite club competition where he became a true legend.

He had already won the Champions League in 2008 with United, and went on to win it four more times with Real.

The first was in 2014 before a remarkable three times in a row in 2016, 2017 and 2018 (beating Liverpool in the Gareth Bale/Loris Karius final) to become the first player to win the Champions League five times.

Since his departure, former Real team-mates Toni Kroos, Dani Carvajal, Luka Modric and Nacho have gone on to win six.

Cristiano Ronaldo had a penalty saved by Gavin Bazunu before netting twice to deny Ireland a famous win in Faro

Ali Daei scored 109 goals for Iran between 1993 and 2006 - and it was felt like maybe his world record for international goals in men's football would never be broken.

But Ronaldo's two late headers in a World Cup qualifying win over the Republic of Ireland in 2021 took him onto 111 goals.

He kept adding to that total and finished on 146 goals in 234 caps - also a record for international appearances.

Cristiano Ronaldo was the first player in professional football to ever hit 900 official goals

Ronaldo continued to smash the goals in for Juventus, in his second spell at United and at Al-Nassr but failed to really replicate many truly magic moments of the past.

However he did create some history in 2024 as he became the first player to score 900 top-level career goals as Portugal beat Croatia.

That number is now 985 - so he is only 15 off an unprecedented 1,000th goal.

He has now hit five for Sporting, 450 for Real Madrid, 145 for Manchester United, 101 for Juventus, 138 for Al-Nassr and 146 for Portugal.

He recently confirmed that he is aiming to hit the 1,000 mark.

But old rival Messi is on 931 goals, the second highest scorer ever, so Ronaldo cannot afford to dawdle too much...

#741. What new Kane deal means for England and the Premier League record

England captain Harry Kane scored scored 213 times in 320 league games for Tottenham

Harry Kane's decision to sign a new contract with Bayern Munich carries heavy significance for the Bundesliga giants, who have been celebrating his status as a Ballon d'Or winner, but also for England and the Premier League's record books.

Bayern have acted swiftly to secure the 33-year-old on a deal taking him through to 2029 after he was crowned the world's best player, ensuring England's captain and record goalscorer will spend the final peak years of a magnificent career at Allianz Arena.

Kane has written himself into Bayern legend since joining from Spurs for Â£86m in August 2023, scoring 102 goals in 102 Bundesliga matches, winning two league titles and three successive Golden Boot awards.

It is why Bayern could not contemplate his departure as other clubs eyed his next move - and why the announcement Kane is staying casts ripples far beyond Munich.

Does it mean Kane will never grace the Premier League again? And does it mean - far more enticingly - he has his sights set on two more major tournaments and two more chances to grasp the prize that has eluded him at international level?

Former England striker Chris Sutton told BBC Sport: "I certainly think, although you always have to factor fitness issues into all of this, that Harry is more than capable of carrying on for a few years yet, easily.

"People might say his game lacks a little bit of pace, but he's so strong in other areas. He is a world-class all-round player. His finishing isn't going to be affected in any way by his age. He can still link up play and his football brain is first class.

"I don't see his age being such a big deal. You think of pacy players over the years who rely on that part of the game then lose it as they get older. Harry is not one of those. He seems fit and at the peak of his powers with Bayern and England."

Kane's new contract expires shortly before his 36th birthday, certainly raising the prospect the player who left Spurs as the highest scorer in their history with 280 goals in 435 appearances may never grace the Premier League again.

His consummate professionalism, and apparent ability to develop into the complete player with age, means this can never be discounted.

The notion of an emotional return to Spurs at some point has often provided background noise, but now looks increasingly unlikely.

What it surely means is that Alan Shearer will remain the Premier League's highest scorer - who knows what will happen with Erling Haaland as Manchester City await punishment after being found guilty of breaching financial regulations they deny? - and out of Kane's reach.

Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or after 73 goals in 65 games for Bayern Munich and England during the 2025â26 season

Shearer scored 260 goals in 441 Premier League matches for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle United. Kane scored 213 times in 320 league games for Spurs.

With Kane still 47 short of Shearer's record, it would need a spectacular late-career flourish for him to eclipse the Geordie icon's tally to write another entry into the history books, which also have him as England's highest scorer with 91 goals from a record-equalling 125 caps.

What will be of huge interest to Thomas Tuchel - the coach who took him to Bayern and now leads England - is that Kane has delivered a clear indication that Euro 2028, to be played in the UK and Ireland, is firmly in his sights.

And, when this new deal expires, Kane is also only a year away from the 2030 World Cup, to be played in Morocco, Portugal and Spain, with special centenary opening matches held in Uruguay, Argentina, and Paraguay.

This, of course, is a stretch given the inevitable rigours of age, but few who know Kane, who have watched him move to a new level at Bayern, would ever say never to such a driven personality, hiding fierce mental strength and a competitive instinct behind his humble 'anti-superstar' persona.

Sutton said: "Euro 2028 certainly shouldn't be a problem and who knows beyond that? If Harry has got players around him with pace and dynamism, as well as runners in and around him, then his football brain isn't going to change and he can still play a huge part.

"He's such a sharp, quick, thinker. He reads the game superbly, knows where his next pass is going and has shown an ability to drop deep and impact the game.

"Harry just seems to be getting better and more rounded with age. And as for age, just look at someone like Teddy Sheringham. He was playing and scoring goals for West Ham United in the Premier League in his 40s.

"Sheringham was an incredibly talented player with supreme intelligence. Harry Kane falls right into the same category.

"Ronaldo has just retired from international football with Portugal at 41, but he is a totally different player than Harry Kane. Harry is one who can drop a little bit deeper to use his incredible ability and range of passing.

"As well as that ability, it is about how Harry's football brain works as much as anything and that won't change with age."

'My heart was beating so fast' - Kane wins Ballon D'or

And it is an argument, and a hope, that is even more pertinent as England still do not possess any other striker or forward who could be considered anywhere near Kane's class or potency.

"When you talk about 2028 or 2030, who are the English strikers coming through to challenge him to take him out of the team?" said Sutton. "There's no-one in his class or effectiveness, or anywhere near it."

What also plays into the argument that Kane cannot be ruled out of such long-term involvement is the manner in which he responded so superbly to what was a disappointing Euro 2024, not only as England lost in the final to Spain but because he looked a jaded shadow of his old self.

Kane looked so out of sorts there was a clamour for him to be replaced by Ollie Watkins, then at Aston Villa. He was substituted in all of England's knockout matches, including after only 61 minutes of that final loss to Spain in Berlin.

And yet, Kane still finished as the tournament's joint top scorer with three goals from seven games.

The notion of him being replaced with the stakes so high now is unthinkable, such is his peerless form and stature.

While Bayern are convinced their new investment in Kane's brilliance will be rewarded with further honours, Tuchel will hope it is motivation and inspiration to finally end the country's long wait for international glory.

#740. AI agents run this automated biology lab that sequences DNA and more

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Heidi Ledford reports for Nature from Seattle, Washington.

A self-driving lab named AutoDNA can work out the constituent ‘letters’ in a snippet of DNA.Credit: Turtle Rock Scientific/Science Source/Science Photo Library

To say that someone has ‘good hands’ is high praise in a molecular biology laboratory, where researchers must deftly handle delicate glassware, pipette samples and more. But in an unusual genetics lab at Shanghai Jiao Tong University in China, a team of robots driven by artificial intelligence is designing and doing experiments with no hands to speak of.

The facility, described today1 in Nature, is one of the latest steps towards ‘self-driving’ labs that are guided by AI, with minimal input from human scientists. With samples moved around by robotic arms, the Shanghai lab can operate more than 20 types of instrument, complete thousands of operations in a single project and do experiments that involve synthesizing and sequencing DNA, among other tasks.

An experiment is designed and executed from start to finish by a team of AI agents, following a simple prompt from a human operator. After that, human hands are needed only to refresh reagents and to service hardware.

The system, called AutoDNA, is remarkable both for its degree of autonomy and because it can readily incorporate a diverse range of lab equipment, says Milad Abolhasani, a chemical engineer at North Carolina State University in Raleigh. “The future of science is going to involve a lot of autonomous labs.”

Labs have long incorporated automation into their workflows, using machines to conduct specific aspects of experimental protocols, such as mixing and heating chemicals. Now, some researchers are hoping to harness increasingly sophisticated AI tools to create self-driving labs, in which an AI system designs and executes complex experiments, troubleshoots and tweaks protocols, and orchestrates activities across an entire lab that is chock-full of disparate equipment.

Designing such labs for molecular biology is challenging because of the field’s complex workflows, which require assorted equipment and high precision, says Haibo Chen, a computer scientist at Shanghai Jiao Tong University and a co-author of the report. “In many existing systems, human experts are still required to configure the instruments,” he says. “AI is mostly added to handle just one part of the process.”

To create a more fully autonomous lab, Chen and his colleagues decided to construct it from the start with AI in mind, rather than adding AI capabilities to a pre-existing system.

The team tested AutoDNA by tasking it with a variety of projects, including detecting a cancer-linked mutation in a sample of DNA. In another experiment, the researchers asked the system to encode a message in DNA using its four nucleotide bases, abbreviated as A, C, G and T. They selected a popular quote, often misattributed to cosmologist Stephen Hawking: “Intelligence is the ability to adapt to change.”

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03552-8
